stories.title: Ruturaj Gaikwad named West Zone captain for the Duleep Trophy, with Prithvi Shaw earning a recall
stories.what_happened: West Zone's selectors named their squad for the **2026-27 Duleep Trophy**, appointing **Ruturaj Gaikwad** — Chennai Super Kings' IPL captain — as West Zone captain, with Mumbai all-rounder **Shams Mulani** as vice-captain. The 15-man squad also includes Shardul Thakur, Sarfaraz Khan, Musheer Khan, Tushar Deshpande and wicketkeeper Harvik Desai, with six of the fifteen players coming from Mumbai. The headline inclusion is **Prithvi Shaw**, who was left out of Mumbai's squad and instead rebuilt his case with Maharashtra, scoring **537 runs** at an average of **48.81** in his debut season for the new state — form strong enough to earn this zonal recall. The tournament begins **August 23** at the BCCI Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru.
key_points: **Ruturaj Gaikwad** will captain West Zone in the 2026-27 Duleep Trophy, with **Shams Mulani** as his deputy.
**Prithvi Shaw** earns a recall to zonal cricket after a strong debut Ranji Trophy season for Maharashtra — **537 runs** in 11 innings at an average of **48.81**.
The 15-man squad includes six Mumbai players, among them all-rounder **Shardul Thakur** and batter **Sarfaraz Khan**.
The tournament, India's season-opening first-class competition, begins **August 23** at the BCCI Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru.
The announcement follows East Zone naming **Ishan Kishan** captain with 15-year-old **Vaibhav Sooryavanshi** as his deputy.

depth.background: The **Duleep Trophy** is Indian domestic cricket's traditional season-opener, pitting India's regional zones against each other. National selectors have long used it as an early-season form guide before the marquee Ranji Trophy season, which is why the tournament carries extra weight for players trying to force their way back into national reckoning — like Prithvi Shaw, a former India opener who was dropped by his home state, Mumbai, and had to rebuild his case for a new state before zonal selectors took notice.

stories.title: F1 delays final call on its 2026 season finale until September, ruling out a US replacement race
stories.what_happened: Speaking this week, F1 president **Stefano Domenicali** said the sport will make its final decision on the fate of the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix in **mid-September at the earliest** — giving organizers as much time as possible to see whether the security situation in the Middle East stabilizes. He confirmed F1 remains **committed to holding both races as planned** for now, but said that if the conflict makes it impossible, the season will instead end with a race in **Europe** rather than a hastily arranged one in the United States, specifically because a new US race would clash with the **NFL season** and be difficult to schedule around. This follows the earlier cancellation of the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix, which were replaced by a rebranded race at **Sepang, Malaysia** in October.
key_points: F1 president **Stefano Domenicali** says a decision on the season's last two rounds won't come until **mid-September at the earliest**
Any replacement race will be held in **Europe**, not the US — F1 doesn't want to clash with the **NFL season**
The **Qatar and Abu Dhabi** season-closing races are at risk if the **Middle East conflict** makes them impossible to hold safely
F1 says it remains **committed** to holding both races in 2026 for now
This is the second time this season the Middle East conflict has forced a calendar rethink, after **Bahrain and Saudi Arabia's** April races were already cancelled

depth.background: Formula 1's 2026 calendar has already been disrupted once this year: the **Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix**, originally set for April, were both cancelled after the US and Israel's strikes on Iran and the retaliation that followed made the region too dangerous to race in safely. F1 improvised by having **Sepang in Malaysia** host a race under the 'Bahrain Grand Prix' name in October instead. Now the same conflict is threatening the **final two rounds of the season**, in **Qatar and Abu Dhabi**, which are usually the championship-deciding races in November/December.

stories.title: Supreme Court strikes down the rule letting projects get environmental clearance *after* they've already started
stories.what_happened: On **July 29**, a three-judge Supreme Court bench of **Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, and Justice Vipul Pancholi** unanimously **struck down the 2021 Office Memorandum** that had let the Centre grant environmental clearance to projects **after** they had already started construction or operations. The Court held that **prior environmental clearance is the cornerstone** of India's environmental regulatory framework and cannot be sidestepped through an executive order. It ruled the government **does** have the power to permit post-facto clearances, but only if it does so through a **valid statutory notification under Section 3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** — not an internal memo. Clearances already granted under the 2017 notification or the now-scrapped 2021 memo will **continue to hold**, unless separately challenged in court, and the judgment applies **prospectively** — meaning no fresh clearances can be issued through the scrapped route from here on.
key_points: The Supreme Court **quashed a 2021 Office Memorandum** that let projects get **retrospective ('post-facto') environmental clearance**.
A **three-judge bench** led by **Chief Justice Surya Kant** ruled the Centre can't create such a bypass through a mere administrative order.
The Centre **can still allow post-facto clearances**, but only through a **valid statutory notification**, not an office memo.
Clearances already granted under the **2017 notification** and the now-**quashed 2021 memo** stay valid unless individually challenged.
The ruling applies **going forward only** — no new post-facto clearances can be issued under the scrapped mechanism.

depth.background: In India, most large projects — mines, factories, power plants, real estate — legally need an **environmental clearance (EC)** *before* construction begins, to assess and limit ecological damage upfront. Some companies have started projects without this approval and then sought clearance afterward, effectively asking regulators to forgive a fait accompli. In **2021**, the central government issued an **Office Memorandum (OM)** — a lower-level administrative order, not a law — creating a formal process for exactly that kind of after-the-fact approval, which environmental groups and courts have long argued undermines the entire point of the clearance system.

stories.title: F1 sets mid-September deadline to decide fate of Qatar and Abu Dhabi season finales
stories.what_happened: F1 boss Stefano Domenicali confirmed the sport will wait until mid-September at the earliest to decide whether the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix, both scheduled to close out the 2026 season, can be safely held given the security situation in the Middle East. The Bahrain Grand Prix has already been moved to Malaysia in October as a workaround. If a replacement race is needed for Qatar or Abu Dhabi, F1 says it would be held in Europe rather than added to the US leg of the calendar, specifically to avoid clashing with the NFL season. The Saudi Arabian Grand Prix has already been dropped outright, leaving the calendar at 23 races instead of the planned 24.
key_points: F1 chief **Stefano Domenicali** confirmed a **mid-September deadline** to decide if the **Qatar and Abu Dhabi** season-finale races can go ahead
The **Bahrain Grand Prix** has already been relocated to **Malaysia in October** after being scrapped from its original slot
Any replacement race would be held in **Europe**, avoiding a clash with the **NFL season** in the US
The 2026 calendar is already down to **23 races** after the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix was dropped entirely
The disruption traces back to the **Iran-US conflict**, which forced Bahrain and Saudi Arabia off the original April schedule

depth.background: F1's 2026 season was originally planned as a 24-race calendar. The Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix were postponed in April because of the ongoing Iran-US conflict and regional security concerns in the Gulf. An attempt to reschedule one of those races for early October also fell through due to continued instability. Now the season-ending Qatar and Abu Dhabi races face the same uncertainty.

stories.title: Sachin Siwach storms into Commonwealth Games boxing quarter-finals as Lovlina Borgohain gets a bye into hers
stories.what_happened: **Sachin Siwach** won his men's 60kg round-of-16 bout 4-1 on judges' scorecards against England's William Hewitt, advancing to the quarter-finals. Separately, **Lovlina Borgohain**, competing in the women's 75kg category, received a bye straight into her quarter-final — and under Commonwealth Games boxing rules, every fighter who reaches the semi-finals is already assured of at least a bronze medal, so Borgohain's medal is effectively locked in regardless of her next result. These add to India's growing tally after earlier medals from Preeti Pawar, Priya Ghanghas and Jadumani Singh, who also advanced to their semi-finals this week.
key_points: **Sachin Siwach** beat England's William Hewitt 4-1 to reach the men's 60kg quarter-finals.
**Lovlina Borgohain** is already guaranteed a medal after a **quarter-final bye** in the women's 75kg category.
Every Commonwealth Games boxing semi-finalist is guaranteed at least a **bronze medal**.
India's 14-member boxing squad (7 men, 7 women) is competing across **14 medal events** at Glasgow 2026.
The boxing competition runs from **July 24 to August 1**.

depth.background: The **Commonwealth Games 2026** are underway in Glasgow, and India traditionally uses the boxing and wrestling events as major medal sources — though this year's pared-back Glasgow programme has dropped wrestling, badminton, table tennis and hockey altogether, leaving boxing as one of India's strongest remaining medal opportunities. India sent a 14-strong boxing squad (seven men, seven women) to compete across 14 weight-category events.

stories.title: Lewis Hamilton locks in a third season at Ferrari by hitting his contract's performance target
stories.what_happened: Hamilton has now **activated that clause**, securing a guaranteed **third season with Ferrari**, after meeting the contract's performance conditions — helped by his current **P2 championship standing**. The confirmation came in the same period that Ferrari team principal **Fred Vasseur** was openly critical of the team's strategy calls during its most recent race weekend before the summer break, showing the news landed alongside genuine internal frustration rather than an uncomplicated celebration.
key_points: **Lewis Hamilton** has activated a clause guaranteeing him a **third season** at Ferrari.
The clause was written into the contract he signed in **January 2024**, tied to hitting performance conditions.
Hamilton currently sits **P2 in the championship** standings, satisfying the clause's bar.
Team boss **Fred Vasseur** was frank about Ferrari's mistakes over a recent race weekend even as Hamilton's future was confirmed.
It removes uncertainty around one of F1's most closely watched driver-team pairings.

depth.background: **Lewis Hamilton**, a seven-time world champion, left Mercedes to join **Ferrari** — one of the most anticipated driver moves in F1 history — under a contract signed in **January 2024**. Rather than a flat multi-year guarantee, the deal included a **performance-linked clause**: Hamilton would only be guaranteed a third season if he hit certain results-based conditions, giving Ferrari flexibility if the partnership underperformed.

stories.title: Red Bull wants to lock down Max Verstappen through 2029 — right as his contract's exit door swings open
stories.what_happened: Red Bull has opened talks to extend Verstappen's contract by an additional season, from its current 2028 expiry to **2029**, which would give him **14 consecutive seasons** with the team. But the timing is notable: Verstappen's existing deal contains an **exit clause** that activates if he isn't inside the **top two** of the drivers' championship by the summer break — and he is currently **sixth**, meaning he could walk away from Red Bull entirely rather than sign anything new. Reports describe the ball as being in **Verstappen's camp**, with no indication yet of which way he's leaning.
key_points: **Red Bull** is trying to extend **Max Verstappen's** contract, which runs to **2028**, by one more year to **2029**.
That would make it Verstappen's **14th season** with the team if he signs.
Verstappen's current deal has an **exit clause** letting him leave if he's outside the **top two** in the standings at the summer break.
He is currently **sixth** in the championship — meaning that exit clause is now **live**.
The Dutchman **has not yet decided** whether to accept Red Bull's proposed extension.

depth.background: **Max Verstappen** is a four-time Formula 1 world champion who has driven for **Red Bull** his entire F1 career. His current contract was built with clauses tied to on-track performance, reflecting how dominant Red Bull expected to remain — including a clause letting him exit if the team (or he) fell below a certain competitive standard by a set checkpoint in the season. Red Bull's underperformance this year relative to its past dominance has made that clause a live talking point rather than a formality.

stories.title: Congress moves to force a Lok Sabha debate on the Ram Mandir donation-fraud scandal, demands a Supreme Court-judge probe
stories.what_happened: On July 29, Congress MP **KC Venugopal** gave notice of an adjournment motion in the Lok Sabha — a procedural move to halt regular business and force an immediate debate — over what he called "massive financial fraud and embezzlement" of public donations at the Ram Mandir. This follows an earlier letter Venugopal sent Prime Minister Modi around July 20 making the same demand. Congress argues the SIT's arrests so far — **8 low-level staff**, with about **₹80 lakh** recovered from six of them — are "eyewash" that protects more powerful people, pointing to the deletion of **7 to 8 months of CCTV footage** and the earlier removal of a Chief Accounts Officer who had flagged irregularities as far back as **2020–21**. Trust general secretary Champat Rai, who resigned July 6 and was replaced by Bajrang Bangara, has broken his silence to deny personal wrongdoing, saying he will address the allegations in full once the SIT submits its final report.
key_points: Congress general secretary **KC Venugopal** filed an adjournment motion in the Lok Sabha to force debate on alleged **embezzlement of Ram Mandir donations** in Ayodhya
He is demanding an independent inquiry **monitored by a sitting Supreme Court judge**, not the state-run probe already underway
The state SIT has arrested **8 people** — drivers, clerks and outsourced cashiers — recovering roughly **₹80 lakh** in cash and foreign currency, but no senior figure has been charged
Congress says **7–8 months of CCTV footage** was destroyed and a whistleblowing accounts officer was removed years before the scandal broke
Trust general secretary **Champat Rai resigned** on July 6 amid the row and has called the personal allegations against him **"baseless"**

depth.background: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust runs the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, the temple built on a site at the center of decades of religious and political conflict in India and a flagship project closely associated with the ruling BJP and Prime Minister Modi. Since the temple opened, it has drawn enormous cash and jewellery donations from pilgrims. In June, reports surfaced alleging a **coordinated racket siphoning off donations**, prompting Uttar Pradesh's state government to form a **Special Investigation Team (SIT)** on June 13 and register an FIR on June 25. The Trust accepted Champat Rai's resignation on July 6 and began restructuring its administration, including plans to hire a professional CEO.

stories.title: India's Foreign Secretary wraps up a two-day Beijing visit aimed at steadying ties with China
stories.what_happened: Misri began his engagements on **July 28** with a meeting with **Sun Haiyan**, Vice Minister of the International Department of China's Communist Party, where the two discussed implementing guidance from both countries' leaderships to improve relations — including more political engagement, people-to-people contacts, and academic/think-tank exchanges. He then met **Hua Chunying**, China's Vice Foreign Minister, reviewing the full range of bilateral issues and exploring ways to advance the idea that India and China should see each other as **partners rather than rivals**, with a focus on mutually beneficial trade and economic cooperation. The visit concluded on **July 29**.
key_points: Foreign Secretary **Vikram Misri** concluded a **two-day visit to Beijing** on July 29 after a series of high-level meetings.
He met **Sun Haiyan**, Vice Minister of the Chinese Communist Party's International Department, on July 28.
He also met **Hua Chunying**, China's Vice Foreign Minister, to review the 'entire spectrum' of bilateral relations.
Both sides discussed framing each other as **'partners and development opportunities rather than competitors.'**
The visit builds on a **gradual normalization** of ties following the prolonged **India-China border standoff**.

depth.background: India and China, the world's two most populous nations, fought a deadly border clash in the Galwan Valley in 2020 that froze high-level diplomatic and economic ties for years. Relations have been thawing gradually since then, with both sides restoring some direct flights, easing visa rules, and resuming senior-level talks — while the underlying border dispute in the Himalayas remains unresolved. **Vikram Misri**, India's top career diplomat as Foreign Secretary, has been a key figure managing this delicate reset.

stories.title: 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi named vice-captain as Ishan Kishan leads East Zone in the Duleep Trophy
stories.what_happened: East Zone's selectors named wicketkeeper-batter **Ishan Kishan** as captain for the opening Duleep Trophy of the 2026-27 domestic season, with **Vaibhav Sooryavanshi** appointed vice-captain — the teenager's first leadership role in zonal red-ball cricket. Sooryavanshi is expected to **open the batting** alongside the experienced **Abhimanyu Easwaran**. The 15-member squad includes seamers **Mohammed Shami** and **Mukesh Kumar**, while **Riyan Parag** and **Akash Deep** were left out due to injury. The tournament begins **August 23** at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru.
key_points: **Ishan Kishan** will captain **East Zone** in the **Duleep Trophy 2026-27**, India's marquee zonal red-ball tournament.
**Vaibhav Sooryavanshi**, just **15 years old**, is named **vice-captain** — his first leadership role in zonal cricket.
Sooryavanshi is expected to **open the innings** alongside experienced Bengal batter **Abhimanyu Easwaran**.
Pacers **Mohammed Shami** and **Mukesh Kumar** are in the squad; **Riyan Parag and Akash Deep miss out through injury**.
The tournament's opening round starts **August 23** at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru.

depth.background: The **Duleep Trophy** is one of Indian domestic cricket's most prestigious first-class (multi-day, red-ball) tournaments, contested between **zonal teams** (East, West, North, South, Central) rather than state sides, and has historically been a proving ground for players pushing for national selection. **Vaibhav Sooryavanshi** became a sensation as a teenager for his aggressive batting in age-group and franchise cricket, and this vice-captaincy marks a significant step up in responsibility at just 15.

stories.title: Asian Paints' profit jumps 40% as India Inc.'s biggest earnings day gets underway
stories.what_happened: Asian Paints posted **consolidated net profit of ₹1,539.25 crore** for the quarter, up nearly 40% from ₹1,099.77 crore a year earlier. **Revenue from operations rose 17.9% to ₹10,541.94 crore**, and profitability improved too — PBDIT (a measure of operating profit) jumped 33.5% with margins expanding to 20.6% from 18.2%. The stock rose on the back of the print. The same day, Dabur, Adani Enterprises, Adani Ports, Eicher Motors, Waaree Energies and dozens more companies are also due to report, making it one of the heaviest single days of the earnings season.
key_points: Asian Paints' Q1 FY27 net profit rose **40% year-on-year to ₹1,539 crore**.
Revenue climbed **18% to ₹10,542 crore**, with margins improving from 18.2% to **20.6%**.
The results beat estimates and **shares rose** on the print.
Dabur and over **100 other companies**, including Adani Enterprises and Eicher Motors, report the same day.
It's one of the **busiest single earnings days** of this reporting season for Indian markets.

depth.background: India's Q1 (April-June) earnings season is when listed companies report their first-quarter results for the new financial year (FY27), and paint major Asian Paints is one of the most closely watched **consumer-demand bellwethers** because paint sales track housing, renovation and discretionary spending closely. A strong or weak Asian Paints number is often read as a signal for the broader consumer economy, not just the company itself.

thread.previously: We flagged this morning that today was India Inc.'s biggest earnings day of the season, with Asian Paints, Dabur, Adani Enterprises, Adani Ports, Eicher Motors, Waaree Energies and 100+ other companies all due to report Q1 FY27 results.

stories.title: Lando Norris says McLaren hasn't 'fully clicked' with its car yet — despite his first win of 2026
stories.what_happened: Speaking after the Hungary win, Norris admitted the team 'doesn't feel like we have fully clicked with our understanding of this car just yet,' suggesting there's still untapped performance in the current chassis despite the dominant result. He praised the car as 'beautiful to drive' and said Sunday's pace was 'some of the best' he's experienced, while also acknowledging in a separate comment that he'd expected slightly more from the weekend given how the car felt. The remarks came as McLaren looks to build momentum in the second half of the championship.
key_points: Norris says the team still hasn't got **close to the car's full potential**, even after winning at the Hungaroring.
The win came off the back of a **revised rear wing**, first shown in Austria but only raced in Hungary.
It was Norris and McLaren's **first win outside a Sprint since Sao Paulo last year**.
Norris called it 'some of the best pace I've ever had,' saying the **car was 'beautiful to drive.'**
He and the team believe there's meaningfully **more performance left to unlock** for the rest of 2026.

depth.background: Lando Norris took McLaren's **first win of the 2026 season outside of a sprint race** at the Hungarian Grand Prix on **July 26**, starting from his first pole of the year and converting it comfortably. The win followed a run of upgrades McLaren had been rolling out through the season, including a revised rear wing debuted in Austria weeks earlier but held back from racing until Hungary.

stories.title: Sensex jumps over 800 points, Nifty back above 24,200 as IT stocks rally and crude rebounds
stories.what_happened: Indian equity benchmarks opened sharply higher on **Wednesday, July 29**, with the **Sensex jumping 657.85 points (0.85%)** to open at **77,423.77** and the **Nifty gaining 191.3 points** to open at **24,176.65**. By **1:00 PM**, the Sensex was trading at **77,589.82**, up **824.07 points (1.07%)**, while the Nifty rose **243 points (1.01%)** to **24,228.35**. The rally came amid mixed global cues, as crude oil prices rebounded after falling **14% over three sessions** tied to the escalating US-Iran standoff. **Infosys** led the Sensex pack, gaining **3.89%** in early trade, alongside **L&T, TCS, Hindustan Unilever** and **Tech Mahindra**.
key_points: Sensex jumped as much as **824 points (1.07%)** to **77,589.82**; Nifty rose **243 points** to **24,228.35**
**Infosys** led gainers, up nearly **4%** in early trade; L&T, TCS, Hindustan Unilever and Tech Mahindra also rose
The rally came as **crude oil rebounded** after falling **14% over three sessions** on US-Iran tensions
Marks a sharp reversal from **yesterday's flat, slightly negative close** of down ~70 points
**IT stocks** are leading the charge again — the same sector that had cushioned yesterday's small dip

depth.background: Indian benchmark indices track a mix of global cues (US Fed decisions, crude oil prices, foreign investor flows) and domestic earnings season results. Crude oil is especially important for India, which imports roughly 85% of its oil — so when crude prices swing, it directly affects the rupee, inflation expectations, and the profitability of oil-importing sectors. The past week has seen sharp crude volatility tied to the escalating US-Iran standoff in the Middle East, whipsawing sentiment across Indian markets.

thread.previously: Yesterday the Sensex closed marginally lower at 76,765.92 (down about 70 points) and the Nifty slipped to 23,985, with IT stocks like TCS and Tech Mahindra gaining even as PSU banks, FMCG, and chemical stocks dragged the index down.
thread.changed: Today the mood reversed sharply: the Sensex surged over 800 points (about 1.07%) to 77,589 and the Nifty climbed above 24,228, as crude oil rebounding after a 14% three-session drop lifted sentiment, with Infosys leading gainers, up nearly 4% in early trade.

stories.title: Lok Sabha passes tougher anti-paper-leak bill amid uproar over Rahul Gandhi's 'shooting' claim
stories.what_happened: The Lok Sabha passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 by voice vote on Wednesday, despite repeated disruptions. The bill sets stricter penalties — up to **10 years in prison** and fines as high as **₹10 crore**, plus asset confiscation — for those convicted of leaking exam papers or otherwise cheating public examinations. It also imposes firm timelines: leak investigations must be completed within two months, and trials must conclude within three. The debate itself was overshadowed by a separate political clash, after Congress leader Rahul Gandhi accused Home Minister Amit Shah of ordering police to fire on students during a July 20 protest march, which the government denied.
key_points: Lok Sabha passed the **Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026** by voice vote
Punishment rises to up to **10 years in jail** and fines up to **₹10 crore**, with confiscation of assets
New deadlines require paper-leak **investigations to finish in 2 months** and trials in **3 months**
The bill follows nationwide protests over the **NEET-UG 2026** exam leak, which forced education minister **Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation**
Passage came amid a Lok Sabha uproar after **Rahul Gandhi** accused the government of ordering pellet-gun fire on protesting students

depth.background: The bill amends the existing Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, which was already meant to deter exam-paper leaks but has failed to stop repeated scandals. The latest and biggest trigger was the **NEET-UG 2026** medical entrance exam leak, which set off nationwide student protests and ultimately cost education minister Dharmendra Pradhan his job. Union Minister Jitendra Singh introduced the amendment bill days after the protests, and it was taken up for debate this week during Parliament's monsoon session.

thread.previously: We reported that Parliament was debating a tougher anti-paper-leak law carrying up to 10 years' jail and ₹10 crore fines, introduced after the NEET protests.
thread.changed: The Lok Sabha has now actually passed the bill by voice vote, amid a separate uproar over Rahul Gandhi's allegation that the Home Minister ordered students to be shot.

stories.title: Audi's Bortoleto says his 2027 future is 'already sorted' as Sainz's Williams seat stays in doubt
stories.what_happened: Bortoleto confirmed publicly that his position at Audi is locked in beyond 2027, closing off one seat some had speculated Sainz might target. That leaves Sainz weighing his limited options: staying at a struggling Williams, or a long-shot Audi move complicated by Hulkenberg's existing contract through 2027. Separately, reports note Fernando Alonso is likely to stay at Aston Martin through 2027 if the team's competitive form improves, while Franco Colapinto's seat is described as at risk in some team-reshuffle scenarios, with a return to Williams floated as one landing spot.
key_points: Audi driver **Gabriel Bortoleto** says he's signed with the team **'for many years'** and his 2027 seat is settled.
That narrows the field just as **Carlos Sainz** weighs his own future amid **Williams' poor form** since the 2026 rules reset.
Sainz is still linked to **Audi**, but teammate-designate **Nico Hulkenberg** is contracted there through **2027**.
**Fernando Alonso** is likely to stay at Aston Martin through 2027 if the team's form holds up.
**Franco Colapinto** could lose his current seat in some scenarios, with a Williams return floated as a fallback.

depth.background: F1's 2027 driver market is unusually fluid because several teams — Audi (the rebranded Sauber works team), Williams, and Aston Martin — are all still settling their long-term line-ups following the sport's 2026 rules reset, which reshuffled the competitive order. Carlos Sainz joined Williams for 2025 expecting the team to be competitive under new rules, but Williams has struggled, fueling speculation he could look elsewhere for 2027.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi accuses Amit Shah of ordering students to be shot; government denies it
stories.what_happened: During Wednesday's Lok Sabha debate on the anti-paper-leak bill, Rahul Gandhi said Home Minister Amit Shah had 'ordered the shooting of our students' and put 'pellets into the blood of our students' during the July 20 march, triggering a major uproar in the House. Union Minister Jitendra Singh directly rejected the claim, stating no shots were fired and that only tear gas was used to disperse the crowd. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju called the allegation a serious breach of Gandhi's own position and privilege, and demanded he apologise. The exchange repeatedly disrupted proceedings even as the underlying bill was ultimately passed.
key_points: Rahul Gandhi told the Lok Sabha that Home Minister **Amit Shah 'ordered the shooting'** of protesting students
He said police put **'pellets into the blood'** of students during the **July 20 'Sansad Chalo' march** at Jantar Mantar
Minister **Jitendra Singh** rejected the claim, saying **no shots were fired** and only tear gas was used
Parliamentary Affairs Minister **Kiren Rijiju** demanded Gandhi **apologise**, calling it a breach of privilege
The clash erupted during debate on the **anti-paper-leak bill**, tied to the same NEET-UG protest movement

depth.background: The allegation stems from the wave of student protests that followed the NEET-UG 2026 exam-leak scandal. On July 20, students marched on Parliament in a 'Sansad Chalo' demonstration demanding accountability; the government says police used tear gas to control the crowd, while opposition figures have alleged more forceful tactics were used, including pellet guns. Rahul Gandhi, as Leader of the Opposition, has positioned himself as a vocal defender of the protesting students throughout this episode.

stories.title: India's economy sends mixed signals as a weak monsoon and trade shocks offset falling oil prices
stories.what_happened: A Bloomberg review of India's economy published **July 29** found the picture is genuinely mixed: government capital spending has slowed and fewer new infrastructure projects are being announced, both of which usually signal softer near-term growth. At the same time, **June rainfall came in around 40% below normal**, and some forecasters now warn the eventual monsoon shortfall could be worse than the **10% deficit** currently built into official projections — a serious risk given how much of Indian agriculture depends on the rains. Set against that, falling **global oil prices** are helping India, a major crude importer, by lowering its import bill and easing some inflation pressure. The RBI has publicly maintained that the domestic economy remains resilient despite the Iran-war and tariff-related uncertainty.
key_points: **Slow government spending** and fewer new project announcements are weighing on India's growth outlook.
**June rainfall ran ~40% below normal**, with forecasters warning the monsoon shortfall could beat the **10% deficit** currently projected.
A weak monsoon threatens to **curb crop output, push up food prices, and squeeze rural incomes** — a large share of India's population depends on farm income.
The **RBI** (India's central bank) says the economy has stayed **resilient** through the Iran war and tariff shocks so far.
Falling global **oil prices** are a rare tailwind, cutting India's import bill since it buys most of its crude abroad.

depth.background: India's growth engine runs on a delicate balance: strong domestic demand and services growth on one side, and the **monsoon** (June–September rains that irrigate most Indian farmland) and global trade conditions on the other. This year, India is also absorbing the shock of new US tariffs and elevated oil-price volatility tied to the **Iran war**, both of which the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** has flagged as key risks to watch. A poor monsoon hits India differently than most economies because so much of rural income and food-price inflation depends directly on rainfall.

stories.title: Deep depression crosses into Odisha-Bengal near Digha, flash-flood red alert issued for 27 Odisha districts
stories.what_happened: The deep depression crossed the West Bengal coast near Digha shortly after midnight and has since moved west-northwestward over northern interior Odisha and Gangetic West Bengal. The India Meteorological Department issued a **red warning** for Sundargarh, Kendujhar and Mayurbhanj districts for Wednesday, while Odisha's Special Relief Commissioner directed collectors in **27 of the state's 30 districts** to stay on high alert for flash-flood-like conditions. Isolated pockets could see rainfall in excess of **204.5mm**. Schools were shut in several affected districts as a precaution, and fishermen have been told to stay off the northwest Bay of Bengal and the Odisha-Bengal-north Andhra coast through the morning of July 29.
key_points: The system made landfall near **Digha** on the West Bengal coast just after midnight
IMD issued a **red alert** — its highest warning — for Sundargarh, Kendujhar and Mayurbhanj
**27 of Odisha's 30 districts** have been placed on flash-flood alert by the state government
Rainfall could exceed **204.5mm** in isolated pockets through July 29–30
Schools shut in Mayurbhanj, Jagatsinghpur and Kendrapara districts as a precaution

depth.background: This weather system formed over the northwest Bay of Bengal and intensified into a deep depression before crossing the coast — the same system we covered making landfall near Haldia on July 28. Since then it has continued pushing inland across Odisha and Gangetic West Bengal at roughly **12km/h**, dragging its heavy-rain band with it. This comes on the heels of Assam's floods earlier this month, which killed dozens and displaced hundreds of thousands, making this eastern-India monsoon stretch an unusually punishing one.

thread.previously: We reported the system crossed the coast near Haldia on the morning of July 28, with a red alert for three districts and ten Odisha districts flagged for heavy rain.
thread.changed: The system has since pushed further inland, and the flash-flood alert has widened dramatically to 27 of Odisha's 30 districts, with several districts closing schools as a precaution.

stories.title: F1's 2027 driver market domino chain: Alonso's next move could decide seats at Williams, Alpine and Haas
stories.what_happened: Paddock reporting suggests Alonso's decision on where he races in 2027 is now the key that unlocks several other seats. **Franco Colapinto**, currently at Alpine, was seen having dinner with Williams team principal **James Vowles**, fuelling speculation he could return to Williams — the team he raced for in 2025 — if Alonso takes over his Alpine seat. Separately, **Esteban Ocon's** position at Haas looks vulnerable: he has scored only **3 points** this season compared to teammate **Ollie Bearman's 13**. Both **Carlos Sainz** and Ocon are being mentioned as candidates to replace Alonso at **Aston Martin** if he leaves. Meanwhile **Sergio Perez** is reportedly being evaluated by three different teams — Williams, Aston Martin, and Alpine — as a fallback signing.
key_points: **Fernando Alonso's** choice of team for 2027 is expected to trigger a **domino effect** across several grids
**Franco Colapinto** was seen dining with Williams boss **James Vowles** — a hint he could return there if Alonso takes his Alpine seat
**Esteban Ocon's** Haas seat looks shaky after just **3 points** this season versus teammate **Ollie Bearman's 13**
**Carlos Sainz** and **Esteban Ocon** are both floated as possible replacements for Alonso at **Aston Martin**
**Sergio Perez** is being eyed as a fallback option by **three teams** — Williams, Aston Martin and Alpine

depth.background: Formula 1's driver market runs on a web of interlocking contracts — when one high-profile driver moves, it frequently forces a chain reaction as teams scramble to fill the resulting vacancy, and the drivers who lose out chase the next-best seat elsewhere. Going into the 2026 season's back half, a wave of contracts are expiring for 2027, and **Fernando Alonso**, a two-time world champion now racing for Alpine, is one of the biggest names still undecided about his future — making him the trigger point for several other teams' plans.

stories.title: Shubman Gill becomes India's fourth-ever No.1 ranked ODI batter as Siraj tops the bowling charts too
stories.what_happened: Following his performances in India's recent ODI series in England — including an unbeaten 80 in the first match and 77 at Lord's in the third — **Shubman Gill** overtook Babar Azam to claim the **No.1 spot in the ICC ODI batting rankings**, becoming just the fourth Indian to do so after Sachin Tendulkar, MS Dhoni and Virat Kohli. In the same rankings update, **Mohammed Siraj** rose to **No.1 among ODI bowlers**, giving India the top spot in both disciplines at once. Separately, 15-year-old **Vaibhav Suryavanshi** jumped 230 places in the T20I batting rankings, reflecting his rapid rise through IPL and youth-cricket performances.
key_points: **Shubman Gill** dethroned Babar Azam to become the world's **No.1 ranked ODI batter**.
**Mohammed Siraj** simultaneously rose to **No.1 among ODI bowlers**.
Gill is only the **fourth Indian ever** to hold the top ODI batting spot, after Tendulkar, Dhoni and Kohli.
The rise came on the back of Gill's England ODI series form, including scores of **80 not out and 77**.
Teenager **Vaibhav Suryavanshi jumped 230 places** in the T20I batting rankings on the same list update.

depth.background: The **ICC Player Rankings** are updated regularly using a points system that weighs recent performances, opposition strength and match context, and reaching No.1 in any format is considered one of the clearest statistical markers of a player's current form. Gill has been closing in on the top ODI spot for weeks; Babar Azam had held it before him.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones hit a Russian city again, damage a 7th Wildberries warehouse; woman killed in Taganrog
stories.what_happened: Ukrainian drones struck **industrial facilities in Ryazan**, a city roughly 200 km southeast of Moscow, on **July 29**. The regional governor said the strikes started fires and that **six people** required medical attention. Among the sites hit was a **Wildberries warehouse** — the **seventh** of the e-commerce giant's facilities damaged in a wave of recent attacks. In a separate incident the same day, a **woman was killed** and a man injured in the southern port city of **Taganrog** on the Sea of Azov, after **missile debris** struck an apartment building. Russian authorities confirmed both incidents.
key_points: Ukrainian drones struck **industrial sites in Ryazan**, a Russian city southeast of Moscow, sparking fires
A **Wildberries warehouse** was damaged — the **7th** of the Russian retailer's facilities hit in recent days
**Six people** in Ryazan sought medical attention after the strikes, the regional governor said
Separately, a **woman was killed** and a man injured when **missile debris** struck an apartment building in **Taganrog**
Part of Ukraine's escalating **'deep strike' campaign** targeting Russian industrial, logistics, and energy sites

depth.background: Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in **February 2022**, both sides have increasingly used long-range drones and missiles to strike targets far from the front line — Russia hitting Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure, and Ukraine hitting Russian oil refineries, military plants, and now warehouses and logistics hubs. Through 2026 Ukraine has scaled up these '**deep strike**' attacks, aiming to disrupt the Russian economy and supply chains that support the war effort rather than just battlefield targets. Wildberries, one of Russia's largest online retailers, has seen a string of its warehouses damaged in these strikes in recent days, making it a recurring target.

stories.title: Hamilton says Ferrari must close a straight-line speed gap to fight for the F1 title in the second half
stories.what_happened: Heading into Formula 1's summer break, **Hamilton** is second in the drivers' championship, **50 points** behind leader **Kimi Antonelli**, and **31 points** behind Ferrari teammate **Charles Leclerc**, who won the **British Grand Prix** this year while Hamilton took his own win at the **Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix** in June. Hamilton said Ferrari's main weakness has been straight-line speed, estimating the car has been **three to four tenths of a second down** on power and pace compared to rivals for the season's first half. He pointed to Ferrari winning **two of the last three races** as evidence the team is closing that gap, and said he feels **more focused than ever** going into the second half of the season.
key_points: Hamilton sits **second** in the drivers' championship, **50 points** behind runaway leader Antonelli
He's just **31 points** behind teammate **Charles Leclerc**, who won the **British Grand Prix**
Hamilton says Ferrari has been **three to four tenths down** on the straights in pace and power all season
Ferrari has won **two of the last three races**, a sign the car is closing the competitive gap
Hamilton says he's '**more focused than ever**' heading into the season's second half

depth.background: Formula 1's season splits into two halves around a summer break, giving teams a rare pause to regroup and plan upgrades before the run to the championship. **Lewis Hamilton**, a seven-time world champion, joined Ferrari for the 2025 season hoping to end the team's long title drought; his 2026 campaign has been solid but not dominant, sitting behind both championship leader Kimi Antonelli and his own teammate Charles Leclerc for parts of the year.

stories.title: Ryan ten Doeschate returns to Knight Riders as head of cricket strategy across all franchises
stories.what_happened: Knight Riders Sports announced Ryan ten Doeschate as its new Head of Cricket Strategy, a role that will oversee scouting, player recruitment, squad planning and performance evaluation across its four global franchises: Kolkata Knight Riders in the IPL, Trinbago Knight Riders in the CPL, Abu Dhabi Knight Riders in the ILT20, and Los Angeles Knight Riders in the MLC. Alongside the strategy role, he will also work as assistant coach for the CPL, ILT20 and MLC teams specifically. The appointment follows his exit as assistant coach of the India men's team, a position he held for two years. He was a title-winning player for KKR in IPL 2012 and 2014, and was part of the support staff for their third title in 2024.
key_points: **Ryan ten Doeschate** is Knight Riders Sports' new **Head of Cricket Strategy**, overseeing scouting and squad planning across all its teams
That covers **Kolkata Knight Riders (IPL)**, **Trinbago Knight Riders (CPL)**, **Abu Dhabi Knight Riders (ILT20)** and **Los Angeles Knight Riders (MLC)**
He'll also serve as **assistant coach** for the CPL, ILT20 and MLC franchises in the group
The move comes right after he **stepped down as India men's team assistant coach**, a role he held for two years
Ten Doeschate previously won **two IPL titles as a KKR player (2012, 2014)** and a third as **support staff in 2024**

depth.background: Knight Riders Sports is the ownership group behind Kolkata Knight Riders and its sister T20 franchises in the Caribbean Premier League, ILT20 and Major League Cricket. Ten Doeschate's ties to the group go back to 2011 as a KKR player, and he later moved into coaching there in 2022 before joining India's men's team as assistant coach for two years, a post he has now left.

stories.title: Assam flood toll climbs to 75 as seven more die in Sivasagar, 3.32 lakh people affected
stories.what_happened: Assam's government confirmed the flood death toll has reached **75** after **seven** more people drowned in **Sivasagar district**. More than **3.32 lakh (332,000) people** remain affected across seven districts — Sivasagar, Charaideo, Golaghat, Jorhat, Nagaon, Sonitpur and Kamrup Metropolitan. In response, Chief Minister **Himanta Biswa Sarma** announced an increase in compensation for families of the deceased to **₹9 lakh**, and said more than **one lakh** of the worst-affected households have already received **₹15,000** each in immediate cash relief.
key_points: Assam's flood death toll has risen to **75** after **seven** fresh drowning deaths in Sivasagar district
More than **3.32 lakh people** remain affected across **seven districts**
Chief Minister **Himanta Biswa Sarma** raised compensation for bereaved families to **₹9 lakh**
Over **one lakh** severely-hit households have received **₹15,000** each for immediate relief
Sivasagar, Charaideo, Golaghat, Jorhat, Nagaon, Sonitpur and Kamrup Metropolitan remain the worst-hit districts

depth.background: Assam floods almost every monsoon season (roughly **June to September**) as the Brahmaputra river and its tributaries swell with heavy rain and water flowing down from upstream in the eastern Himalayas. The state's low-lying floodplains, dense population, and river-erosion patterns mean floods regularly displace hundreds of thousands of people and damage crops, roads and homes. This year's flooding has been building for weeks, with the death toll climbing steadily as more casualties are confirmed from remote, hard-to-reach areas.

stories.title: Bumrah's Sri Lanka Test fate now hinges on an August 7 practice match in Colombo
stories.what_happened: New reporting details the specific mechanism that will decide whether **Bumrah** plays in India's upcoming Sri Lanka Test series: a **practice match in Colombo beginning August 7** is now understood to be the actual test of his readiness, rather than a simple fitness scan. That leaves only **eight days** between that practice match and the first Test, which starts **August 15 in Galle** (the second Test follows August 23 in Colombo). Bumrah has been resting his knee since injuring it fielding in the second ODI against England at Cardiff, with medical staff advising a full rest period until **July 30** before he reports to the BCCI's **Centre of Excellence** in Bengaluru for rehab and reassessment. All-rounder **Ravindra Jadeja**, who had also been on a fitness watch after an IPL 2026 elbow injury, has already been cleared and is back in the squad.
key_points: A **practice match in Colombo starting August 7** will be the real decider on Bumrah's fitness
That's just **eight days** before the first Test begins in **Galle on August 15**
Bumrah hurt his knee fielding in the **second ODI vs England** in Cardiff; swelling ruled him out of the third
He was told to **rest until July 30**, then report to the BCCI's **Centre of Excellence** in Bengaluru
**Ravindra Jadeja** has already been declared fit and is back in the squad after IPL 2026 elbow trouble

depth.background: Jasprit Bumrah is India's premier fast bowler, and his fitness has been carefully managed for years due to a history of back and workload issues. He picked up a knee injury while fielding during the second ODI against England in Cardiff, and it worsened enough to rule him out of the following match. India's squad for the upcoming two-Test tour of Sri Lanka — captained by Shubman Gill, with KL Rahul as deputy — was already named on July 26, with Bumrah included but explicitly marked as fitness-dependent, and Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna named as pace backups in case he isn't ready.

thread.previously: As of two days ago, Bumrah was resting his injured knee until July 30 before reporting to the BCCI's Centre of Excellence for a fitness scan, with multiple reports suggesting he was unlikely to be fit in time for the two-Test series starting August 15 in Galle.
thread.changed: It has now emerged that a practice match in Colombo starting August 7 — just eight days before the series opener — will be the real test of his fitness, leaving a very tight window to build match fitness before Galle.

stories.title: India Inc.'s biggest earnings day of the season: Asian Paints, Dabur and 100+ companies report today
stories.what_happened: Wednesday, July 29 is one of the year's busiest results days, with **Asian Paints, Dabur India, Adani Enterprises, Adani Ports, Eicher Motors and Waaree Energies** among the companies due to report Q1 FY27 numbers. Brokerages expect **Asian Paints** to show 14–17% year-on-year revenue growth on the back of 2–4% price hikes taken in June and dealers stocking up ahead of them, though margins may come in flat to slightly lower as crude-linked raw material costs rose during the quarter. **Dabur** has already signaled roughly double-digit revenue and profit growth in a pre-results update, with India volumes up about 5% and rural demand outpacing urban demand for a second consecutive quarter. The pace continues into Thursday, July 30, when over 100 more companies — including Bajaj Finance, Tata Steel, Mahindra & Mahindra, Sun Pharma, Maruti Suzuki and Swiggy — report.
key_points: **Over 100 companies** report April–June (Q1 FY27) results today, one of the season's busiest days
Asian Paints is expected to post **14–17% revenue growth**, helped by price hikes, though margins may stay flat
Dabur has flagged **roughly double-digit** revenue and profit growth, with **rural demand outpacing urban** for a second straight quarter
Adani Enterprises, Adani Ports and Eicher Motors are also among today's reporters
**Thursday (July 30) is even bigger** — Bajaj Finance, Tata Steel, Maruti Suzuki and Sun Pharma are all due

depth.background: Indian companies report earnings quarterly, and **Q1 FY27** covers April–June 2026 (India's financial year runs April to March, so this is the first quarter of FY2026-27). Results days routinely bring sharp, stock-specific price swings as investors react to whether numbers beat or miss expectations, separate from the broader index-level moves driven by macro news like Fed decisions or oil prices.

stories.title: Iran says US strikes wrecked Bushehr airport, killed over 350 government workers
stories.what_happened: Iran's government published a detailed account of infrastructure destroyed by US strikes over the past two weeks. It says **Bushehr airport is completely inoperable** and a newly purchased aircraft was destroyed there, along with damage to the Bandar Abbas railway and airports at Iranshahr, Semnan and Bandar Abbas. The government also claims **more than 350 of its employees were killed**, though this figure has not been independently confirmed by outside observers. Separately, Russia has pulled another 163 staff out of the nearby Bushehr nuclear plant as a precaution, leaving about 300 personnel there. The US has not officially confirmed casualty figures or commented on this specific report.
key_points: Iranian officials say US strikes destroyed **Bushehr airport**, which they say must be rebuilt from scratch
The government says **over 350 government employees** were killed in the campaign — a toll Reuters says it could not independently verify
**12 bridges**, two tunnels, a marine control tower and a weather station were also damaged, per Tehran
Russia has evacuated **163 more staff** from Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant, leaving roughly 300 personnel still on site
This is Iran's **first detailed public accounting** of war damage since the informal pause took hold

depth.background: The US and Iran have been in an undeclared conflict since February 2026, triggered by Iranian-linked attacks on shipping in the **Strait of Hormuz** — the narrow waterway through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes. The US and allies responded with strikes on Iranian military sites and infrastructure. Fighting has recently eased into an informal pause, but Tehran has refused to sign onto any formal ceasefire, leaving the truce fragile. Russia, which helped build and staff Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant, has a direct stake in how the damage assessment plays out.

thread.previously: We reported that the US-Iran fighting had settled into an uneasy pause, but that Tehran was refusing to call it a formal ceasefire.
thread.changed: Iran's government has now released its first detailed public damage report from the two-week bombing campaign: Bushehr airport destroyed, over 350 government employees dead, and dozens of bridges, tunnels and other infrastructure hit.

stories.title: Delhi Capitals gatecrash the Hardik Pandya trade talks, offering Axar Patel and Prithvi Shaw
stories.what_happened: The Pandya trade saga has taken a new turn: Mumbai Indians' initial ask of **Shivam Dube and Ayush Mhatre** from Chennai Super Kings hit a wall when CSK refused to part with Mhatre, a rising young batter, instead countering with **Dube, South African batter Dewald Brevis, and ₹10 crore in cash**. With that standoff unresolved, **Delhi Capitals** have stepped into the picture, reportedly willing to offer both **captain Axar Patel and opening batter Prithvi Shaw** to land Pandya. Should the MI-CSK talks collapse over valuation, **Kolkata Knight Riders** have also emerged as a potential destination for Pandya.
key_points: **Delhi Capitals** have entered trade talks for Hardik Pandya, offering **Axar Patel and Prithvi Shaw**.
**Mumbai Indians** wanted Shivam Dube and Ayush Mhatre from CSK in return for Pandya; **CSK refused to include Mhatre**.
CSK's counter-offer: **Dube, Dewald Brevis, and ₹10 crore cash** instead.
**Kolkata Knight Riders** have emerged as a fallback destination if the MI-CSK deal collapses entirely.

depth.background: Hardik Pandya has captained **Mumbai Indians** since returning to the franchise, but reports of trade talks with **Chennai Super Kings** first surfaced as CSK looks to rebuild around experienced leadership. IPL trade windows allow franchises to swap contracted players outside the annual auction, and a captain-level trade of Pandya's stature would be one of the biggest moves of the IPL 2027 cycle.

stories.title: A brush-on liquid stopped tooth decay in more than half of treated baby teeth in a major US trial — no drilling required
stories.what_happened: Researchers led by the **University of Michigan** ran a randomized Phase III clinical trial enrolling **830 children younger than 6**, recruited through dental offices, pediatric medical practices, and Head Start / Early Head Start programs across Michigan, New York, and Iowa. Children in the trial had a **38% SDF solution** brushed directly onto their decayed baby teeth every six months. The study, published in **JAMA Pediatrics**, found the treatment arrested decay in **more than half** of the treated teeth — stopping the cavity from getting worse without any drilling, injections, or sedation. The one tradeoff: SDF permanently **stains the treated area black**, since it works partly by reacting with the tooth's minerals. Researchers say this is the kind of large US population trial the FDA needs to formally evaluate SDF as an approved drug for treating cavities, rather than an off-label technique.
key_points: A **Phase III trial of 830 children** under 6 found that silver diamine fluoride (SDF) arrested decay in **more than half** of treated baby teeth
The treatment is a liquid **brushed onto the cavity in seconds** — no drilling, needles, or sedation needed
It was tested at **6-month intervals** using a **38% SDF** solution
Led by the **University of Michigan**, recruiting through dental and pediatric offices and Head Start programs in Michigan, New York, and Iowa
The trial gives the FDA the large-scale US safety and efficacy data it needs to formally approve SDF as a **drug** for treating cavities

depth.background: Cavities in baby teeth are extremely common, and the standard fix — drilling out the decay and filling it — is often traumatic for young children, sometimes requiring sedation or general anesthesia. **Silver diamine fluoride (SDF)** is a liquid that has been used for decades in other countries, including Japan, as a simple way to stop decay from spreading without removing any tooth material. It has lacked the large, rigorous **US clinical trials** regulators need before approving it as an official treatment, which is why many American dentists have only offered it informally or as a stopgap.

stories.title: US and Saudi Arabia strike Iran-backed sites in Iraq after a fresh wave of drone attacks
stories.what_happened: CENTCOM said US and Saudi aircraft struck multiple **logistics and weapons sites in eastern Iraq** on Tuesday evening, July 28, in response to more than **30 drone attacks directed by the IRGC** against US-linked positions over the prior three days. The response came hours after Iran's own ballistic missile attack on US forces was intercepted, and roughly a day after President Trump said Washington had halted its bombing campaign because Iran 'wanted to talk' — a claim Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei publicly disputed, saying **'we have no negotiations with the United States at present.'** CENTCOM added that '**the IRGC and its terrorist proxies must cease these attacks to avoid further US military response.**' Iranian officials condemned the Iraq strikes as a dangerous escalation and a breach of Iraqi sovereignty. Trump, writing online, warned Iran not to counter-attack, saying the US would respond with **'a force that has never been seen.'** The exchange followed closely on Trump's White House meetings with Israeli PM Netanyahu and Ukraine's Zelensky, both described by the administration as 'positive and productive.'
key_points: US and Saudi fighter jets hit **logistics and weapons sites** in eastern Iraq used by Iran-backed militias
The strikes answered **more than 30 drone attacks** on US-linked targets over the previous 72 hours
Trump publicly warned Iran '**THEY BETTER NOT**' retaliate, threatening a response 'never before seen'
Iran called the joint strikes a '**highly dangerous escalation**' and a violation of Iraqi sovereignty
The renewed fighting came **a day after** Trump said the US had paused its bombing campaign on Iran

depth.background: Since a wave of **Iranian ballistic missiles targeted US forces in the Middle East on July 28** (intercepted, no injuries, oil jumped about 5%), the region has swung between brief pauses and fresh flare-ups. The underlying conflict began after Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (**IRGC**) and allied militias in Iraq, Lebanon and Yemen escalated attacks on US and Israeli-linked targets, and Washington answered with strikes of its own. Iraq's Kurdistan region has separately absorbed a string of Iranian drone and missile strikes on Kurdish dissident camps this month, showing how the fighting keeps spilling beyond Iran's own borders. Trump has run a dual track — talking about negotiations one day, ordering strikes the next — which both sides say has made the situation genuinely unpredictable.

thread.previously: Iran's IRGC fired up to four ballistic missiles at US forces in the Middle East on July 28; all were intercepted with no injuries, and oil jumped about 5% on fears the recent calm was fraying.
thread.changed: The US and Saudi Arabia hit back directly, striking Iran-backed logistics and weapons sites in Iraq in response to over 30 IRGC-directed drone attacks in 72 hours, and Trump issued a public warning against any Iranian counter-strike.
