stories.title: Nvidia in talks to guarantee $250 billion of OpenAI's mega Ohio data-center debt
stories.what_happened: The **Wall Street Journal** reported that Nvidia is in talks to provide a roughly **$250 billion** financial guarantee that would let OpenAI lease a planned **10-gigawatt** data-center campus in southern Ohio, being developed by SoftBank's energy arm. A guarantee like this effectively means Nvidia is promising to cover the debt if OpenAI can't, making it much easier for OpenAI to borrow the money in the first place. Beyond the guarantee, Nvidia is reportedly discussing a **separate $350 billion** financing arrangement specifically to fund the semiconductor chips that would go inside the facility. All-in, people familiar with the plan estimate the total project cost — land, buildings, power, and chips — could exceed **$500 billion**. Only the first phase, about 800 megawatts of capacity, is scheduled to be ready by **2028**; the full 10-gigawatt build-out would take much longer. As of the report, the deal terms were not finalized and could still change.
key_points: Nvidia is negotiating a **$250 billion** guarantee so OpenAI can lease a giant **10-gigawatt** data-center campus SoftBank is building in Ohio.
Counting the Nvidia chips that would fill it, the whole project could cost more than **$500 billion** — one of the largest single AI infrastructure bets ever made.
Nvidia is separately discussing a further **$350 billion** financing package just to pay for the chips themselves.
The first phase, only **800 megawatts** of the planned 10 gigawatts, isn't due to finish until **2028** — this is a bet on AI demand years out, not today.
Nothing is signed yet: **terms are still being negotiated**, and the deal could still shrink or fall apart.

depth.background: Building the giant computer centers ('data centers') that run AI models like ChatGPT costs an enormous amount of money — for land, power supply, cooling, and above all the specialized chips (GPUs) that do the computing. **OpenAI**, the company behind ChatGPT, has committed to building far more computing capacity than it can currently afford outright, so it increasingly relies on its partners to help finance it. **Nvidia**, which makes most of the world's AI chips, has been doing exactly that: investing in and financially backstopping the very companies that buy its chips, including OpenAI and AI startup Safe Superintelligence. Critics call this 'circular financing' — money moving in a loop between a chipmaker and its customers — because it can make AI demand look stronger than it organically is.

stories.title: Assam becomes the second state to drop all NEET-UG protest cases against demonstrators
stories.what_happened: The Assam government announced it will withdraw all cases and legal proceedings filed against people who took part in protests over the NEET-UG paper-leak controversy. Five cases had been registered in the state, resulting in 13 arrests. The state said that after considering the circumstances and the need for systemic reform in the exam and higher-education system, it decided **no adverse legal action** will be taken against anyone who protested before 6pm on July 26, and instructed police statewide not to pursue further action. Assam is the second state, after **Bihar**, to reverse its legal crackdown on NEET-UG protesters this way.
key_points: Assam's government ordered the **withdrawal of all cases** against people arrested during protests over alleged **NEET-UG exam-paper irregularities**.
**Five cases** had been registered in the state, leading to the arrest of **13 people**.
Police across Assam have been told not to take **any further legal action** against protesters who took part before 6pm on July 26.
Assam follows **Bihar**, which had already dropped similar NEET-UG protest cases — a pattern of states rolling back crackdowns.
The move comes as Parliament separately debates a tougher **anti-paper-leak bill** in response to the same scandal.

depth.background: **NEET-UG** is India's national entrance exam for medical college admissions, taken by over a million students a year. Allegations of paper leaks and other irregularities in this year's exam triggered protests across several states, with students and opposition parties demanding accountability and a re-test. Police response to some of these protests — including the use of force — became a controversy of its own, feeding into a broader national debate this month about how the government polices student demonstrations (a related issue is playing out over the Delhi Parliament-march protests, where the use of Rapid Action Force pellet guns is now facing a Supreme Court-ordered probe).

stories.title: Bombay High Court lets Union minister Nitin Gadkari sue Meta, Google and X over deepfake videos
stories.what_happened: The Bombay High Court permitted Nitin Gadkari, the Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways, to file a civil defamation suit against **Meta Platforms, Google LLC, X Corp** and unidentified others over AI-generated deepfake videos and manipulated posts. The content falsely portrays Gadkari as personally responsible for, and financially benefiting from, the E20 ethanol-blending programme — allegations his petition calls **'false, fabricated and misleading.'** Gadkari's plea states that ethanol-blending policy is administered solely by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, and that he has no role in implementing it. The suit seeks court orders directing the platforms to remove, disable, and prevent further circulation of the content, arguing it has caused serious and lasting harm to his reputation.
key_points: The **Bombay High Court** granted Union minister **Nitin Gadkari** permission to file a civil suit against **Meta, Google and X** over AI-generated deepfake content.
The videos falsely link Gadkari to India's **E20 ethanol-blended petrol programme**, alleging he personally profited from it.
Gadkari says the E20 and ethanol-blending policies are run solely by the **Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas**, not his own Road Transport Ministry.
His suit asks the court to order the platforms to **remove and block** the circulation of the deepfake content.
It's one of the higher-profile tests yet of whether Indian courts will force global platforms to act fast on AI deepfakes targeting public officials.

depth.background: India's **E20 programme** blends 20% ethanol into petrol nationwide, a policy meant to cut fuel imports and emissions; it has also drawn public complaints about reduced mileage and engine concerns, making it a lightning rod for online criticism. Deepfakes — AI-generated videos or images that convincingly show someone saying or doing things they never did — have become a growing legal and political problem in India, with several public figures targeted this year. Gadkari, a senior BJP minister, has previously described the criticism of E20 as a 'paid campaign' against him.

stories.title: Honda's upgraded F1 engine gets an early test outing days before its official debut
stories.what_happened: Honda will introduce its upgraded power unit at an Aston Martin **filming day** this Wednesday at the Hungaroring, giving it a rare chance to gather real running data before the engine's official grand-prix debut. Under F1's sporting regulations, filming days are limited to **200 kilometres** of running on special Pirelli demonstration tyres, using a car in a previously-used specification — so teams cannot treat them as full development tests, but they can verify basic systems integration. The upgrade is aimed at fixing a season in which Honda's power unit has lacked performance and suffered fragile reliability. Honda says it is working towards the engine's full race-weekend debut at the **Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort** in September, the first race after F1's August summer shutdown.
key_points: **Honda** will run its upgraded F1 power unit at an **Aston Martin filming day** on Wednesday at the Hungaroring.
It's an early data-gathering run ahead of the engine's full **grand-prix debut at the Dutch GP** at Zandvoort in September.
F1 rules cap filming days at just **200km** of running on special demo tyres, so it's not a full development test.
The move follows a **torrid 2026 season** for Honda, whose engine has been dogged by weak power and reliability problems.
Honda has been using this year's new **ADUO development-token rules** to build extra horsepower into the upgrade.

depth.background: Honda returned to Formula 1 in 2026 as **Aston Martin's** engine partner, part of a broader relaunch that also brought design chief **Adrian Newey** on board and paired drivers **Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll**. F1 caps how much teams can change their engines mid-season to control costs, but a scheme called **ADUO (Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities)** lets manufacturers earn limited extra upgrade tokens this year — which is how Honda is building a more powerful revised engine mid-season rather than waiting for 2027.

stories.title: Sudan's Army Retakes Key Highway as El-Obeid Braces for a Possible Genocide-Level Siege
stories.what_happened: Sudan's army announced Sunday it had regained full control of the Al Sadarat highway, the main road linking Khartoum to El-Obeid, after driving out RSF fighters who had held it. The army said the operation inflicted heavy losses on RSF troops and forced them to retreat from towns along the route. Controlling the highway lets the army move troops, weapons, fuel and supplies into the besieged city and cuts off one of the RSF's main routes for pushing toward it. Even with the highway recaptured, El-Obeid remains encircled and under near-daily drone bombardment from both sides, striking markets, schools, water infrastructure and fuel stations. The UN's human rights chief, Volker Türk, has publicly warned that the city's civilians are being subjected to 'relentless' attacks as fears grow of a full RSF ground assault.
key_points: Sudan's army said it recaptured the **Al Sadarat highway** linking capital Khartoum to **El-Obeid** on Sunday, after two days of fierce fighting with the paramilitary **Rapid Support Forces (RSF)**.

El-Obeid, capital of North Kordofan state, has swelled to roughly **500,000** people as displaced Sudanese flee into it — and it remains besieged, with UN investigators warning it could become the next **El-Fasher**.

In just three weeks in June alone, the UN documented **15 drone strikes** on El-Obeid that killed at least **45 civilians**; drone strikes by both sides have killed over **1,000** people across the wider Kordofan region since January 2026.

A UN Fact-Finding Mission ruled on **July 9** that RSF's mass killings, gang rape and deliberate starvation during its 18-month siege of El-Fasher amounted to **genocide** against the non-Arab Zaghawa and Fur communities.
Food prices in besieged El-Obeid have surged by as much as **300%**, and residents say they can no longer afford to eat or to flee the city.

depth.background: Sudan has been at war since **April 2023**, when the regular army (SAF) split violently from its former partner, the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), in a struggle for control of the country. The war has displaced more people than any other conflict on Earth and left around **5 million** Sudanese facing emergency or catastrophic hunger. Earlier this year the RSF captured El-Fasher, the capital of North Darfur, after an 18-month siege marked by mass killings later ruled to be genocide by UN investigators — a precedent that has raised alarm that El-Obeid, Kordofan's regional capital, could suffer the same fate.

stories.title: Verstappen brands Racing Bulls drivers 'morons' after blue-flag system failure costs him time
stories.what_happened: Mid-race, Verstappen caught up to lap Lawson and Lindblad, who were battling each other for their own position and went side-by-side into a corner instead of immediately yielding. That cost Verstappen time as he pushed for a strong finish. He erupted over team radio, demanding the pair be penalized and calling them 'morons.' It later emerged the blue-flag light-panel system in the cars had malfunctioned, so race control had to revert to manual marshalling with flags — meaning several drivers, including Lawson and Lindblad, may not have clearly seen the signal telling them to move over. Given the technical failure, stewards issued no penalty to either Racing Bulls driver. Verstappen crossed the line second behind Norris, while Lawson finished eighth and Lindblad tenth, both inside the points.
key_points: Verstappen ripped into Racing Bulls pair **Liam Lawson** and **Arvid Lindblad** on untelevised radio, calling them **'morons'** for not yielding while he tried to lap them
Cause: a **light-panel system failure** meant blue flags weren't showing properly in cockpits, forcing marshals to fall back on manual flag-waving
His exact radio quote: *"Oh, they should get a penalty. This is f***ing ridiculous, these morons! My God"*
Verstappen still finished **P2**, 15 seconds behind winner Lando Norris, so the delay didn't cost him the podium
**Race control took no action** against either Racing Bulls driver once the system fault came to light; Lawson (P8) and Lindblad (P10) both scored points

depth.background: A blue flag (shown on track and as a light on the steering wheel) tells a lapped, slower car to immediately let a faster leader through. Racing Bulls is Red Bull's junior sister team, developing young talent like rookie Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson, but the two squads race as full rivals on track. Verstappen, Red Bull's four-time champion, is fighting to close ground in a title race Mercedes rookie Kimi Antonelli currently leads.

stories.title: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 3,000 cases, spreading faster than any Ebola outbreak on record
stories.what_happened: The Democratic Republic of Congo's health ministry has now confirmed more than **3,075 Ebola cases and 1,354 deaths** since the outbreak began, spread across five provinces including Ituri (the hardest-hit, with roughly 90% of cases) and North Kivu. Case numbers have accelerated sharply, adding about 1,000 new confirmed cases in just the ten days before July 27 — a pace doctors say outstrips prior DRC outbreaks. In mid-July, a crowd angered by a hospital death stormed the **Nyakunde hospital** in Ituri province, forcing Ebola patients and responding medical staff — including the aid group Samaritan's Purse — to flee, and some too-sick-to-move patients were left without treatment. The **UN peacekeeping mission (MONUSCO)** has since deployed a base near Nyakunde to help protect health workers going forward. The virus has also spread beyond DRC's borders: Uganda has confirmed 20 cases, and individual patients have been medically evacuated to Germany and France for treatment.
key_points: Confirmed cases have passed **3,075**, with **1,354 deaths**, across **five provinces** of the Democratic Republic of Congo.
The outbreak hit **1,000 confirmed cases in just 40 days** — the 2018 North Kivu outbreak took **235 days** to reach the same mark.
Roughly **1,000 new cases were added in just the last 10 days**, prompting doctors to describe it as spreading '**like wildfire**.'
An angry mob **attacked a hospital in Nyakunde**, forcing Ebola patients and medical staff to flee, disrupting the response in the worst-hit province.
The virus has already **crossed borders**, with imported cases confirmed in Uganda, and travelers evacuated to Germany and France for treatment.

depth.background: Ebola is a severe, often-fatal viral disease spread through contact with bodily fluids of infected people; the strain driving this outbreak is the **Bundibugyo virus**, one of several Ebola-family viruses. The Democratic Republic of Congo has dealt with Ebola outbreaks before — including the 2018-2020 North Kivu outbreak, one of the worst in history — so the country has real experience and infrastructure for fighting it. This is the DRC's **17th recorded Ebola outbreak**, but responders say it is moving unusually fast: security problems in the eastern provinces, where armed groups operate and distrust of health workers runs high, have repeatedly disrupted containment efforts, including attacks on treatment centers and burial teams.

stories.title: Deportation protections for 300,000+ Haitians in the US expire today, and ICE is ready to move
stories.what_happened: The US Court of Appeals for the DC Circuit's temporary block on revoking Haitian TPS status expires today, after the court pushed the deadline back multiple times since late June while weighing the government's case. Unless a last-minute order intervenes, roughly **300,000 Haitians** living legally in the US under TPS lose that protection and their work permits starting today. US Immigration and Customs Enforcement has been preparing targeted operations to arrest and deport Haitian migrants, according to internal documents reported by CBS News, with Ohio — home to a large Haitian population in cities like Springfield — identified as an early target. The Supreme Court already cleared the way for this on **June 25**, in a ruling that also stripped protections from about 6,000 Syrians, so today's expiry is procedural rather than a new legal decision. Affected migrants can accept a government-funded flight and a $2,600 payment to leave voluntarily, or risk arrest and forced deportation. An estimated 145,000 of the affected Haitians live in Florida alone, including roughly 36,000 in health care roles.
key_points: A federal appeals court's temporary block on ending **Temporary Protected Status (TPS)** for Haitians expires **today, July 27**, clearing the way to strip protections from roughly **300,000 Haitians**.
ICE has been preparing targeted enforcement operations, including in **Ohio**, home to a large Haitian community, with deportation flights reportedly able to begin within days.
The **US Supreme Court** already ruled on **June 25** that the administration could proceed with ending TPS for Haiti and Syria, so today's deadline is the last of three court-ordered delays.
Roughly **145,000** of the affected Haitians live in Florida, including about **36,000** working in health care.
Migrants who leave voluntarily can be offered a government-funded flight home plus a **$2,600** payment.

depth.background: Temporary Protected Status lets people from countries hit by war, disaster, or crisis live and work in the US legally, without a path to citizenship, as long as their home country's designation stays active. Haiti has held TPS for over a decade because of gang violence, political collapse, and a 2021 earthquake that made large parts of the country unsafe to return to. The administration moved to end Haiti's TPS status earlier this year, arguing conditions no longer justify it — a decision challenged in court as endangering people who fled genuine danger. The Supreme Court sided with the administration on **June 25**, but a federal appeals court kept issuing short extensions, pushing the deadline back three times, with today marking the final one's expiry.

stories.title: Houthi drones strike Saudi Arabia's main east-west oil pipeline, widening the Yemen war's reach into the kingdom's oil backbone
stories.what_happened: On Monday, Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had launched drone strikes on facilities along Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline, known as Petroline, which moves oil roughly 1,200 km from the kingdom's eastern fields to the Red Sea port of Yanbu. The pipeline normally runs at its full capacity of **7 million barrels a day** and exists partly so Saudi Arabia can export oil without routing tankers through the Strait of Hormuz. Saree said the attack targeted supply and transport points, framing it as retaliation for repeated Saudi drone flights over Yemeni territory. Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Defense confirmed its air defenses intercepted and destroyed several drones, with no reported casualties or disruption to pipeline flows. This is the third major Houthi strike on Saudi oil infrastructure within a week, after attacks on Aramco's Jizan and Yanbu refineries on July 25 briefly pushed Brent crude above $100 a barrel. Shipping through the nearby Bab el-Mandeb Strait has already fallen to its lowest level in months as vessels avoid the area.
key_points: Yemen's Houthi rebels launched drone strikes today targeting Saudi Arabia's **Petroline**, the pipeline that carries **7 million barrels a day** from eastern oil fields to the Red Sea port of Yanbu.
Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said the strikes hit pumping and transport points, calling it retaliation for **repeated Saudi drone incursions into Yemeni airspace**.
Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Defense said its air defenses **intercepted and destroyed** the attacking drones before any damage.
It follows Houthi strikes on Aramco refineries in **Jizan and Yanbu** days earlier that sent Brent crude above **$100 a barrel**.
The Houthis have also declared a **naval blockade** of Saudi ports this month, marking a sharp escalation from the years-long truce.

depth.background: Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi movement held an uneasy truce for several years after a brutal civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis seized Yemen's capital Sanaa and a Saudi-led coalition intervened to back the internationally recognized government. That truce unraveled this month after a Saudi strike on Sanaa's airport aimed at stopping an Iranian plane from landing, provoking the Houthis into firing missiles at Saudi Arabia and declaring a **blockade** of its ports. The Houthis are part of Iran's regional network of allied armed groups, and their return to open conflict has opened a new front in the wider **US-Israel-Iran confrontation** that has dominated the region this year. Saudi Arabia's oil infrastructure was last hit at this scale roughly four years ago.

thread.previously: Houthi strikes on two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea sent Brent crude above $100 a barrel for the first time since May, before prices eased back to around $97-98 by July 24.
thread.changed: The Houthis have now struck Saudi Arabia's main East-West pipeline directly rather than tankers at sea — hitting fixed oil infrastructure inside Saudi territory, though Saudi air defenses say they intercepted the drones this time.

stories.title: Nvidia stock jumps as its $500 billion South Korea chip deal starts paying off
stories.what_happened: SK Group -- South Korea's second-largest conglomerate -- and Nvidia announced a partnership worth more than $500 billion covering both new AI data centers and a long-term memory-chip supply deal. SK Telecom will build a 2-gigawatt AI computing facility using Nvidia's upcoming Vera Rubin chip platform, running on advanced HBM4 memory made by SK Hynix, with the first facility due online in 2027. On Monday, Nvidia's stock jumped more than 3% as investors reacted positively, even though SK Hynix's own share price stayed largely flat.
key_points: Nvidia and SK Group struck a partnership worth $500+ billion for AI infrastructure
SK Telecom will build a 2-gigawatt AI data center using Nvidia's next-gen chips
SK Hynix is locked in as Nvidia's long-term AI memory-chip supplier
Nvidia shares jumped over 3% Monday; SK Hynix's own stock barely moved

depth.background: Nvidia's AI chips are only as fast as the memory feeding them data, and the world depends on a small number of Asian chipmakers -- mainly SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron -- for that memory. Building AI 'factories' (giant data centers packed with chips) also needs huge amounts of electricity and construction, which is why Nvidia increasingly partners directly with power and telecom companies instead of just selling chips to them.

stories.title: China's industrial profit growth slows to its weakest pace this year
stories.what_happened: Data released Monday by China's National Bureau of Statistics showed industrial profits rose 15.1% year-on-year in June, down from May's 21.1% gain - a second consecutive month of slowing growth as easing energy prices removed some of the tailwind behind this year's rebound. First-half profits are up 18.7%.
key_points: Industrial profits rose 15.1% year-on-year in June, down from 21.1% in May
Second straight month of deceleration as energy and oil prices ease
H1 2026 profits are still up 18.7%, a strong number but slightly down from Jan-May's 18.8%
An AI-driven boom in chip and equipment manufacturing had been a key growth driver this year

depth.background: China's industrial profits swung from barely-positive growth in 2025 to double-digit gains this year, helped by an AI-driven boom in chip and equipment manufacturing and the tail end of nearly three years of factory-gate deflation - falling wholesale prices that had been squeezing manufacturers' margins.

stories.title: Red Bull dangles an ownership stake to stop Verstappen walking to a rival
stories.what_happened: Multiple reports say Red Bull is trying to head off an exit by restructuring Verstappen's contract: extending it a further year to 2029, removing the exit clause entirely, raising his reported base salary (around €65m), and — most strikingly — potentially offering him an equity stake in the team itself, something no active F1 driver has ever held.
key_points: Red Bull reportedly open to extending Verstappen's deal by a year, to 2029
Talk of an equity stake that would make him the most powerful driver in F1 history
His current deal lets him leave if he's outside the top two in the standings at the summer break
Comes right after a shaky Hungarian GP where Red Bull admitted it hasn't built him a car to attack with

depth.background: Max Verstappen is a four-time world champion contracted to Red Bull through 2028 — but with an unusual 'performance exit clause': a get-out that lets him leave early if the team isn't delivering, tied to where he stands in the championship at the summer break. Red Bull's car has struggled to match the front-runners this season, which is exactly why that clause has become the story of the year, with rivals like Mercedes and McLaren circling.

stories.title: Honda's next-gen F1 engine gets its first real test — two years before it matters
stories.what_happened: Fresh off the Hungarian Grand Prix, where Aston Martin's new B-spec AMR26 car showed a clear step in pace, Honda will run an updated version of its power unit for the first time at a filming day at the Hungaroring this Wednesday. Reserve driver Jak Crawford will do the running, limited to 200km under filming-day rules. It's a shakedown ahead of the engine's official race debut at the Dutch Grand Prix in Zandvoort on August 21-23.
key_points: Honda will run its updated power unit at an Aston Martin filming day at the Hungaroring on Wednesday
Reserve driver Jak Crawford does the running, capped at 200km
It comes right after Aston Martin's B-spec car showed a clear pace jump at the Hungarian GP
The engine's official race debut is at Zandvoort, August 21-23

depth.background: Honda officially became Aston Martin's power-unit partner starting in 2026, ending its long Red Bull partnership. F1 rules cap pre-season and in-season track running tightly, so teams use 'filming days' — technically for promotional footage — to sneak in real engineering mileage on new parts.

stories.title: China's Moonshot AI releases the full weights of its Kimi K3 model today, sharpening the fight over 'open' AI
stories.what_happened: Moonshot AI says it is releasing Kimi K3's full model weights today, July 27 — the actual downloadable parameters, not just cloud access. That makes it far easier for developers and researchers everywhere, including in the US, to run and study the model directly on their own hardware. The release follows a chaotic two weeks in which demand for Kimi K3 overwhelmed Moonshot's computing capacity, forcing the company to briefly halt new subscriptions.
key_points: Moonshot AI is releasing Kimi K3's full downloadable parameters today, July 27
The 2.8-trillion-parameter model rivals GPT and Claude on many benchmarks — for free
Demand overwhelmed Moonshot's servers, forcing a brief subscription pause
US officials and Anthropic accuse Moonshot of 'distilling' American models; Moonshot denies it

depth.background: Kimi K3 first appeared in mid-July from Beijing-based Moonshot AI, a relatively unknown startup, and stunned the AI world by nearly matching the best US systems on many tests while being free to use. It's an 'open-weight' model, meaning anyone can download and run its underlying parameters rather than only accessing it through a paid API — the AI equivalent of open-sourcing the recipe, not just selling the finished dish. US officials, alarmed at how fast Chinese labs are closing the gap, have accused Moonshot of 'distillation' — training its model by learning from the outputs of American models like GPT and Claude, a shortcut that's controversial but hard to prove. Days ago, over 50 US tech and policy figures signed a letter urging Washington not to overreact and to keep supporting America's own open-weight AI efforts rather than simply trying to block China's.

thread.previously: We reported that over 50 US tech and policy figures signed a letter urging Washington to keep supporting America's own open-weight AI development rather than simply moving to block Chinese models, as the US weighed curbs on them.
thread.changed: The Chinese model at the center of that debate, Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, released its full downloadable weights today, escalating exactly the dynamic the letter warned about — a free, open Chinese alternative undercutting paid US AI products.

stories.title: Masood's gritty fifty leads Pakistan's fightback on Day 3 in Trinidad, but Babar falls late
stories.what_happened: Pakistan extended their reply through Day 3, built on a 155-run second-wicket partnership between Imam-ul-Haq and captain Shan Masood after Imam was caught at slip. Masood slowed down in the evening session to see out the day unbeaten on 88, but West Indies fast bowler Jayden Seales struck late to remove Babar Azam. Pakistan closed the day on 199/3, still trailing West Indies' 311 by 112 runs, with Salman Ali Agha new at the crease.
key_points: Pakistan closed Day 3 at 199/3, trailing West Indies' first-innings 311
Shan Masood unbeaten on 88, anchoring after a 155-run stand with Imam-ul-Haq
Babar Azam fell late to Jayden Seales after playing a supporting role
Salman Ali Agha is the new man in, yet to score

depth.background: We reported that West Indies were bowled out for 311 on Day 2 of this first Test in Tarouba, Trinidad, with Pakistan reaching 60/1 in reply at that day's stumps. The five-day match, part of Pakistan's tour of the West Indies, runs July 25-29.

thread.previously: We reported West Indies were bowled out for 311 on Day 2, with Pakistan reaching 60/1 in reply at stumps.

stories.title: Supreme Court rules the accused has no right to a lawyer's continuous presence during police interrogation
stories.what_happened: A two-judge Supreme Court bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta modified custody conditions that a trial court had imposed, and an Andhra Pradesh High Court had partly upheld, in the case of a suspended police inspector accused over a custodial death. Interpreting Section 38 of the BNSS, the bench held that the law guarantees an arrested person's right to **meet** an advocate of their choice during interrogation, but does not require that advocate to be **continuously physically present** through every moment of questioning. The Court reasoned that stretching the provision that far would make routine police investigation impractical, while still affirming that safeguards against custodial abuse must remain intact in some form.
key_points: The Supreme Court ruled that **Section 38 of the BNSS** guarantees only the right to **meet** a lawyer, not their **constant physical presence**.
The bench of Justices **Vikram Nath** and **Sandeep Mehta** issued the ruling while deciding a **custodial-death case** against a suspended police inspector.
The Court said custody safeguards **cannot be so strict** that they make police investigation impractical.
**BNSS** (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita) replaced India's colonial-era **CrPC** as the country's criminal procedure code in **2024**.

depth.background: India replaced its 160-year-old criminal procedure code, the CrPC, with a new law called the **BNSS** in 2024, and courts are still working out exactly what several of its provisions mean in practice -- this is one of the first major Supreme Court rulings interpreting Section 38, which deals with an arrested person's access to a lawyer. The case arose from a lower court granting police custody of a suspended police inspector accused in a custodial-death investigation, where the trial court had tried to impose strict conditions -- including a lawyer's continuous presence -- on how police could conduct the interrogation. India's courts have long balanced two competing concerns in custody cases: protecting arrested people from abuse in police custody, and not tying investigators' hands so tightly that they can't actually investigate.

stories.title: Sonam Wangchuk leaves hospital after his 26-day hunger strike, heads to Rajghat before returning to Ladakh
stories.what_happened: Wangchuk walked out of Medanta Hospital in Gurugram on Monday, July 27, days after his health seriously deteriorated during a **26-day hunger strike** that began June 28 at Jantar Mantar. He lost roughly 8 to 10 kg over the course of the fast. He ended the strike on July 24 after the central government agreed to accept all his demands relating to the paper-leak scandal, breaking his fast with juice offered by Union Health Minister JP Nadda at his bedside. Hospital officials said he is now on a liquid diet and in stable health. After discharge, Wangchuk said his first stop would be Rajghat to pay tribute to Mahatma Gandhi — mirroring a visit he made there just before starting the fast — before he heads home to Ladakh to resume his environmental and education work.
key_points: Climate activist **Sonam Wangchuk** was discharged from Gurugram's **Medanta Hospital** after ending a **26-day hunger strike**.
He lost an estimated **8 to 10 kg** during the fast, which he began at Jantar Mantar in support of students hit by the **NEET paper-leak scandal**.
He broke his fast on **July 24** after the central government agreed to **all his demands**, with Union Health Minister JP Nadda present to offer him juice.
His first stop after discharge is **Rajghat**, Mahatma Gandhi's memorial, before he returns home to **Ladakh**.
It echoes his own history: Wangchuk visited Rajghat before starting the fast too, and was previously **jailed for six months** in connection with earlier Ladakh statehood protests.

depth.background: Sonam Wangchuk is a well-known Indian engineer-turned-education-and-climate activist from Ladakh, famous for inventing low-cost solar-heated buildings and for inspiring the engineer character in the film *3 Idiots*. He has spent years campaigning for **Ladakh statehood and Sixth Schedule protection** (special constitutional safeguards for tribal areas), and was jailed for six months earlier in 2026 over related protests before his release in March. In late June he began a fresh hunger strike at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, this time over the **NEET exam paper-leak scandal** and alleged irregularities in CBSE's on-screen marking process, which had triggered nationwide student protests and a police crackdown that Parliament has been fighting over for days.

stories.title: IMD red alert: a deep depression is set to cross the Odisha-Bengal coast today, schools shut in three districts
stories.what_happened: IMD said a deep depression over the northwest Bay of Bengal, close to the West Bengal-north Odisha coast, is expected to move north-northwestwards and cross the coast between Balasore and Canning around the afternoon of July 27. A red alert for extremely heavy rainfall is in force, and schools are shut in Mayurbhanj, Jagatsinghpur and Kendrapara.
key_points: A deep depression over the northwest Bay of Bengal is set to cross the coast near Balasore and Canning this afternoon
IMD has issued a red alert - its highest warning level - for extremely heavy rainfall
Schools are shut in Mayurbhanj, Jagatsinghpur and Kendrapara districts
Fishermen have been told to stay off the sea until the system passes

depth.background: Odisha and coastal West Bengal sit in a monsoon-season corridor that regularly sees low-pressure systems form over the Bay of Bengal and cross the coast, bringing intense rain and flash-flood risk. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) grades these warnings green, yellow, orange or red by severity, with red being the most serious.

stories.title: India's Commonwealth Games athletics campaign opens with a high-jump duel: Kushare vs Tejaswin
stories.what_happened: India's athletics campaign at the Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow begins today with a three-way men's high jump final featuring Kushare, Shankar and Aadarsh Ram Jothi Shankar. It's the headline event of the day as India also has three weightlifting finals underway at the SEC Armadillo.
key_points: India's CWG 2026 athletics campaign in Glasgow opens today with the men's high jump final
National record holder Sarvesh Kushare faces former record holder Tejaswin Shankar
Kushare arrives on the back of a bronze at the Monaco Diamond League
Tejaswin won India's only CWG high-jump medal, bronze, at Birmingham 2022

depth.background: Tejaswin Shankar won India's only Commonwealth Games high-jump medal, a bronze, at Birmingham 2022, before shifting focus in recent years toward the decathlon. Sarvesh Kushare then broke Shankar's eight-year-old national record with a 2.31m leap in Bhubaneswar and has been in career-best form since, most recently taking bronze at the Monaco Diamond League.

stories.title: Government introduces a tougher anti-paper-leak bill in Lok Sabha as NEET fallout continues
stories.what_happened: Union Minister of State Jitendra Singh moved to introduce the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 in the Lok Sabha today. The bill reportedly makes seven changes to the 2024 law, including strict time limits for both police investigations and court proceedings in paper-leak cases, aimed at closing enforcement gaps exposed by the NEET-UG case. Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju has urged MPs to take part in a full discussion on the bill, expected in the House tomorrow.
key_points: Union Minister Jitendra Singh introduces the Public Examinations Amendment Bill, 2026
It tightens the 2024 anti-paper-leak law with faster investigations and trials
Comes days after the education minister resigned over the NEET-UG leak row
Discussion on the bill is expected in the House tomorrow

depth.background: India passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act in 2024 to punish exam paper leaks and organised cheating rackets after a string of scandals. That law is now being tested by this year's alleged NEET-UG medical entrance exam leak, which triggered weeks of student protests, a police crackdown at a Delhi march, and the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan — replaced by Pralhad Joshi, as we reported yesterday. The government had promised tougher exam-security legislation as part of its response.

thread.previously: We reported that PM Modi had put Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani in charge of a new task force to reform India's exam system, alongside Modi announcing fast-track courts for the NEET paper-leak scandal.
thread.changed: Beyond task forces and courts, the government has now introduced actual legislation in Lok Sabha — the Public Examinations Amendment Bill, 2026 — to tighten the law itself, with a full debate expected tomorrow.

stories.title: Supreme Court agrees to hear pleas on police 'excesses' against NEET protesters, but rejects an urgent listing
stories.what_happened: A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant is hearing two petitions today alleging that Delhi Police used disproportionate force — tear gas, lathi charges and other measures — against students protesting the NEET paper-leak issue on July 20. The court had initially declined a request for an urgent, out-of-turn hearing, with the Chief Justice reportedly telling the petitioners' lawyer not to waste the court's time, but agreed the matter would be taken up in the ordinary course today. Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for the petitioners, argued the police response amounted to 'police excess... going against students.'
key_points: CJI Surya Kant's bench will hear two pleas on the July 20 Delhi police crackdown today
Court had earlier declined to list the matter urgently, telling lawyers 'please don't waste our time'
Petitions allege tear gas and lathi-charge were used against NEET paper-leak protesters
Case is separate from the government's talks with protest leaders and the new anti-paper-leak bill

depth.background: Student protests over an alleged leak in this year's NEET-UG medical entrance exam have been building for weeks under the banner of the 'Cockroach Janta Party,' culminating in a 'Chalo Sansad' march toward Parliament on July 20 that Delhi Police broke up with tear gas and lathi charges — injuring, by some accounts, dozens of protesters and police alike. One young woman critically hurt in that crackdown was taken off ventilator support and is now stable, as we reported yesterday. Two separate petitions were then filed asking the Supreme Court to examine whether the police used excessive force.

stories.title: Government holds its first direct talks with NEET protest leaders — but makes no commitments
stories.what_happened: Union Health Minister JP Nadda met a CJP delegation at his residence — the first direct negotiation between the government and protest leaders since the crackdown. The delegation submitted a written memorandum and appealed to protesters to end their sit-in. Nadda said he would raise their concerns 'at the appropriate level' but offered no firm commitments. CJP leaders say the protest continues until remaining demands — ₹1 crore compensation for families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide amid the scandal, and the release of hospitalized activist Sonam Wangchuk — are met.
key_points: Union Health Minister JP Nadda met a CJP delegation for the first negotiation since the Chalo Sansad crackdown
The group submitted a written memorandum and asked protesters to end their sit-in
CJP says no real commitments were made; the protest continues
Remaining demands: ₹1 crore compensation for NEET-related suicide victims and activist Sonam Wangchuk's release from hospital

depth.background: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) has led a weeks-long protest movement over alleged irregularities in India's NEET medical entrance exam, including a paper-leak scandal. Protesters tried to march on Parliament in a 'Chalo Sansad' demonstration; police used a lathi charge to disperse the crowd, critically injuring a woman who was later taken off ventilator support — a story we've covered. Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, one of the protesters' original targets, has since resigned and been replaced by Pralhad Joshi.

thread.previously: We reported a woman critically injured in the police crackdown on the Chalo Sansad march had been taken off ventilator support and was conscious and stable.
thread.changed: The government held its first direct negotiation with CJP protest leaders since the crackdown, but made no firm commitments — the protest continues over compensation and Sonam Wangchuk's release.

stories.title: Netanyahu heads to the White House for a tense Trump meeting, with Iran splitting the two leaders
stories.what_happened: Netanyahu departs for Washington today ahead of a Tuesday meeting with Trump, his sixth Oval Office sit-down since Trump's return to office and his first since the Iran war escalated. The two leaders are expected to clash over next steps on Iran: Netanyahu is pushing for a renewed round of military strikes, while **Trump** — who ordered a halt to two weeks of nightly US bombing raids on Iran last week — is said to prefer giving diplomacy more room. Ahead of the trip, Netanyahu has made conciliatory gestures on Gaza and Lebanon that Israeli commentators read as an attempt to arrive in Washington looking like a cooperative partner rather than a source of friction. While in Washington, Netanyahu will also attend the funeral of **Senator Lindsey Graham**, a longtime Israel ally in Congress. The meeting lands at a delicate moment: the fragile US-Iran halt in hostilities is only days old, and how the two leaders align — or don't — could determine whether it holds.
key_points: Netanyahu meets Trump at the White House on **Tuesday**, his first visit since the Iran war began.
It will be his **sixth** Oval Office meeting with Trump in a year and a half — more than any other world leader.
Iran is the central divide: Netanyahu wants **renewed military action**, Trump leans toward **diplomacy**.
The visit comes days after the US paused its **two weeks of nightly airstrikes** on Iran.
Netanyahu will also attend the funeral of **Senator Lindsey Graham** while in Washington.

depth.background: Since the Iran conflict escalated, the US and Israel have coordinated closely but not always agreed on how far to push militarily. The US carried out nightly strikes on Iran for two weeks before pausing them last week as **Trump** signaled he wants room for diplomacy. Netanyahu has now visited the Trump White House **five times before** this trip, reflecting how central the US alliance is to Israel's wartime strategy — but this is his first visit since the Iran war intensified.

stories.title: China's Moonshot AI releases Kimi K3, the largest open-weight AI model ever built
stories.what_happened: Beijing-based Moonshot AI released the open weights for **Kimi K3**, a **2.8-trillion-parameter** AI model, making it downloadable for free roughly **a day earlier** than the company's own July 27 target. The model uses a 'sparse mixture-of-experts' design, meaning it only activates a small slice of its total parameters for any given task, which keeps inference costs down compared to a dense model of the same size. It supports a **1-million-token context window**, letting it process entire codebases or large document sets in a single pass. On independent benchmarks, K3 ranked behind only Anthropic's and OpenAI's top models on general intelligence, while beating other rivals, including Anthropic's Opus-tier model, on coding and agentic tasks specifically. Moonshot priced API access at **$3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens** — the highest of any Chinese lab, but still roughly half the cost of Anthropic's premium model for comparable work.
key_points: Kimi K3 has **2.8 trillion parameters**, making it the largest open-weight AI model released to date.
Moonshot AI shipped the free download **a day early**, at roughly 7:30pm EDT on July 26.
It only activates a fraction of its parameters per request (a 'mixture-of-experts' design), keeping running costs down despite its size.
It ranks **fourth overall** on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, just behind Claude and GPT's top models but ahead of several others.
Moonshot is charging **roughly half** what Anthropic charges for its priciest model, undercutting Western rivals on price.

depth.background: 'Open-weight' models are AI systems whose trained parameters are published for anyone to download and run, unlike 'closed' models such as those from OpenAI or Anthropic, which are only accessible through a paid API. Chinese AI labs, including Moonshot AI, have leaned into open-weight releases partly because **U.S. export controls limit their access to the most advanced computer chips**, making it harder to compete purely on raw compute — so they compete on giving the model away and letting the ecosystem build on it instead. Moonshot's prior model, Kimi K2.6, was already a well-regarded open-weight system; K3 is a major step up in scale.

stories.title: Gunmen kill at least 30 in a midnight raid on Naridon village in Kaduna State
stories.what_happened: At around 11 pm on Sunday, July 26, gunmen invaded Naridon village in Kauru Local Government Area of Kaduna State, firing indiscriminately at residents before setting houses and shops ablaze. At least **30 people were killed, including 8 children**, and several more were injured; recovery teams warned the toll could climb further. The attackers reportedly operated for hours without being confronted. Residents said military units stationed roughly two kilometres away in nearby Kamaru and Ungwan Magaji did not arrive in time to stop the killing, and that only a single soldier and four Mobile Police officers were deployed to the community afterward. The Kaduna state government has condemned the attack and ordered security agencies to hunt down those responsible.
key_points: Gunmen attacked Naridon village around **11 pm on Sunday**, shooting residents and torching homes.
At least **30 people are dead, including 8 children**, with search teams fearing the toll could rise.
Nearby military posts were just **2 kilometres away** but reportedly did not respond during the hours-long attack.
Only **one soldier and four police officers** were stationed in the village after the killings.
The state government has ordered a **manhunt** and called the attack 'barbaric'.

depth.background: Naridon sits on the border between Kaduna and Plateau states, a stretch of central Nigeria known as the 'Middle Belt' where farming communities (mostly Christian) and herding communities (mostly Muslim Fulani) have clashed for years over land and water, a conflict often called the **Southern Kaduna crisis**. Armed groups — sometimes described as bandits, sometimes as militias — have repeatedly raided villages here with little warning and, residents say, little protection. Kaduna's state government has struggled for years to contain the violence despite repeated pledges of tougher security.

stories.title: F1's summer-break report card: Antonelli's rookie masterclass, and a rough half-season for Verstappen
stories.what_happened: With Formula 1 entering its summer break after the Hungarian Grand Prix, mid-season assessments graded every team's performance under this year's new technical rules. Mercedes' 19-year-old rookie **Kimi Antonelli** has been the story of the season, winning six races and taking podiums in all but two starts to become the youngest driver ever to lead the championship at this stage. Mercedes as a team holds a commanding **78-point lead** over Ferrari in the constructors' standings. The bigger shock is at Red Bull, where four-time champion Max Verstappen sits 7th in the drivers' standings without a single win — reports point to Red Bull's car struggling with electrical deployment and its adaptation to the new active-aerodynamics rules, leaving Verstappen relying on pure driving skill to stay competitive. McLaren, which set the pace for much of last season, has also fallen short on both speed and reliability, with Lando Norris trailing Antonelli by 91 points.
key_points: Rookie **Kimi Antonelli**, 19, leads the drivers' championship at the summer break — the **youngest driver ever** to lead the standings, with **six wins** and podiums in all but two races.
**Mercedes** leads the constructors' championship by a wide margin, up **78 points** on second-placed Ferrari at the break.
**Max Verstappen sits 7th** in the standings with **zero wins** so far — a shock given his recent dominance — with Red Bull's new-rules car reportedly lagging Mercedes and Ferrari.
**McLaren**, last year's benchmark team, has lacked both pace and reliability to keep up, leaving Lando Norris **91 points** behind Antonelli.
The grades come at F1's annual **summer break**, the multi-week pause when teams and press traditionally take stock of the season so far.

depth.background: F1 introduced a major overhaul of its technical rules for the 2026 season — new engines and aerodynamics — the biggest regulatory shake-up since 2022, which reshuffled the competitive order and made this year's midpoint report card unusually consequential. The sport's summer break sits roughly at the season's halfway point and gives teams and commentators a natural pause to assess who has adapted best to the new rules before the run to the championship resumes.

stories.title: West Indies bowled out for 311 as Pakistan fight back to 60/1 at stumps on Day 2 in Trinidad

Pakistan then began their reply and closed the day at 60/1, still 251 runs behind but showing the first signs of fighting their way back into the match.

Pakistan reach 60/1 at stumps, trailing by 251
Pakistan took 4 wickets before lunch bowling with the old ball
1st Test at Tarouba runs July 25-29

Ben Duckett named Player of the Match: 75 off 47 balls

stories.title: Nvidia is in talks to guarantee $250 billion for OpenAI's giant new Ohio data center
stories.what_happened: The Wall Street Journal reported Sunday that Nvidia is in talks to provide a roughly $250 billion financial guarantee to help OpenAI lease and finance a massive AI data center campus being built in southern Ohio by a SoftBank Energy subsidiary. The campus is designed to eventually draw 10 gigawatts of power, with an initial 800-megawatt phase due by 2028. Nvidia's guarantee would cover the lease and construction debt, not the chips that go inside; separately, Nvidia is discussing financing up to $350 billion of OpenAI's chip purchases for the same site. Including the chips, the full project could exceed $500 billion, making it the largest data center project ever announced. The power supply is controlled by the US government and funded by Japan under a recent trade agreement, with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick involved in deciding who gets access to that power.
key_points: Nvidia is in talks to guarantee roughly **$250 billion** in financing so OpenAI can lease a giant new data center in **Ohio**.
The **10-gigawatt** campus is being built by SoftBank's energy arm and could cost more than **$500 billion** all-in, including chips.
It would be the **largest data center project ever announced**.
Nvidia is separately discussing financing up to **$350 billion** of the chip purchases for the same project.
Electricity for the site is controlled by the **US government** and funded by Japan under a recent trade deal.

depth.background: OpenAI has been racing to secure enormous amounts of computing power to train and run its AI models, and data centers at this scale — 10 gigawatts is roughly enough electricity for a small country — cost more than almost any lender will finance alone. SoftBank, the Japanese conglomerate and major OpenAI investor, is developing the site through its energy subsidiary. Nvidia's chips power nearly all major AI systems, and increasingly the company is acting less like a component supplier and more like a financier for its biggest customers' megaprojects.

stories.title: F1 stewards rule Sainz 'wholly responsible' for the Piastri crash -- but only fine him half the usual penalty
stories.what_happened: During Sunday's Hungarian Grand Prix, Carlos Sainz's Williams collided with Oscar Piastri's McLaren as Sainz cut back in while battling Fernando Alonso, not realizing Piastri was attempting to pass him at the same moment. Stewards ruled Sainz 'wholly responsible' for the collision but issued only a 5-second penalty -- half the standard punishment -- because Piastri 'was not visible' in Sainz's mirrors and F1's blue-flag warning system had malfunctioned during the race, leaving Sainz without a signal that Piastri was closing in. Piastri, compromised in his fight for the win by the contact, retired from the race shortly after with a separate gearbox failure and said afterward that Sainz needed to 'look in the mirror.'
key_points: Sainz's Williams collided with Piastri's McLaren at Turn 2/3 in the Hungarian GP
Stewards ruled Sainz fully responsible, but gave a reduced 5-second penalty, not the usual 10
A broken blue-flag warning system meant Sainz wasn't told Piastri was coming past
Piastri called it 'one of the dumbest things' he's seen, and retired soon after with a gearbox failure

depth.background: Blue flags are shown to a slower car to tell its driver a faster car is about to lap or overtake, so they can move aside safely. Race stewards -- officials who police on-track incidents -- normally hand out a standard 10-second penalty to a driver judged fully at fault for causing a collision.

stories.title: Yorkshire crush Sussex by 184 runs in a One-Day Cup rout at Hove
stories.what_happened: At Hove, Yorkshire batted first after early rain reduced the match to 48 overs a side, and posted a commanding 325/7. Opener Adam Lyth hit a six off the very first short ball he faced en route to 21 from just seven balls before being caught. The innings was built around a dominant 160-run fourth-wicket partnership between Will Luxton, who scored a century, and Sam Whiteman, who made 74. In reply, Sussex collapsed to 140 all out in 27.5 overs, with seamer Ben Coad taking his maiden five-wicket haul in List A cricket. Yorkshire were awarded a 184-run win under the DLS method used to set fair targets in rain-affected matches.
key_points: Yorkshire posted **325/7** in a rain-shortened 48 overs, built on **Will Luxton's century**.
Luxton and **Sam Whiteman (74)** added **160 runs** together for the fourth wicket.
**Ben Coad** took a maiden List A **five-wicket haul** to help bowl Sussex out for just **140**.
Yorkshire won by **184 runs** on the DLS method, taking maximum points in the group.

depth.background: The One-Day Cup is English domestic cricket's 50-over county competition, running this summer alongside the more high-profile T20 Hundred tournament — it's where county players build List A credentials and it feeds England's broader domestic pathway. Yorkshire and Sussex are two of England's traditional first-class counties.

stories.title: Assam floods have now killed 66 people and affected 6.5 lakh more, as Union Minister Sonowal calls the situation 'extremely critical'
stories.what_happened: Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal visited flood relief camps in Sivasagar district and described the situation as 'extremely critical,' as Assam's flood death toll for the season reached 66 and more than 6.5 lakh people across six districts remain affected. The state is running 274 relief camps and distribution centres, currently sheltering close to 19,000 displaced people, with the National and State Disaster Response Forces (NDRF/SDRF) continuing rescue and relief operations alongside the Centre.
key_points: Death toll from this year's Assam floods has reached 66
Over 6.5 lakh (650,000) people affected across six districts
Sivasagar is worst-hit, with roughly 3 lakh people impacted
274 relief camps are housing nearly 19,000 displaced people; NDRF/SDRF running rescues

depth.background: Assam faces destructive monsoon flooding most years, as the Brahmaputra river and its tributaries swell with heavy rain and overflow their banks across the state's low-lying districts. This year's flood season has been especially severe, compounding an already-active monsoon that has also triggered fresh IMD (India Meteorological Department) rain alerts elsewhere in the country this week.

stories.title: Chamika Karunaratne's 72* off 34 fires Galle Gallants to the top of the Lanka Premier League table
stories.what_happened: Galle Gallants posted 220 for 6, powered by an unbeaten 72 off 34 balls from Chamika Karunaratne, with useful contributions from Sam Harper, Nurul Hasan, Charith Asalanka and Sahan Arachchige. Dambulla Sixers got a promising start from Niroshan Dickwella in the chase but collapsed once wickets started falling, never mounting a serious threat beyond the powerplay, and Galle Gallants moved to the top of the table with eight points.
key_points: Galle Gallants posted 220/6, driven by Karunaratne's unbeaten 72 off just 34 balls
Dambulla Sixers fell well short in the chase after early wickets triggered a collapse
Win takes Galle Gallants clear at the top of the LPL points table with eight points
This is a separate, later match to the Jaffna-Kandy game already in the feed today

depth.background: The Lanka Premier League (LPL) is Sri Lanka's franchise T20 tournament, now in its group stage with teams playing for a spot in the playoffs. Galle Gallants and Dambulla Sixers had already met once this LPL season, when Dambulla won comfortably — making this a rematch with the earlier result at stake.

stories.title: Surrey cruise past Northamptonshire by 6 wickets in the One-Day Cup
stories.what_happened: At Guildford, Northamptonshire batted first and posted 254/8 from their 50 overs. Surrey's batting lineup chased the target down with relative ease, reaching 258/4 in 43.1 overs to win by 6 wickets, with 41 balls to spare — a controlled run-chase rather than a nailbiter.
key_points: Northamptonshire posted **254/8** batting first at Guildford.
Surrey chased it down comfortably, reaching **258/4** in **43.1 overs**.
The win came by **6 wickets**, with **41 balls** still remaining.
It's another group-stage points boost for Surrey in the **2026 One-Day Cup**.

depth.background: This was a Group A fixture in the same 2026 One-Day Cup competition as the Yorkshire-Sussex match — English county cricket's 50-over format, running in parallel with The Hundred this summer.

stories.title: Championship leader Antonelli gets a triple penalty at the Hungarian GP and drops from pole pace to P7
stories.what_happened: During Saturday's qualifying for the Hungarian Grand Prix, Antonelli was investigated for not slowing sufficiently when yellow flags came out for Verstappen's spin — stewards found he lifted off the throttle only slightly and remained **faster through the corner than on his previous lap**, which is the definition of an unfair advantage under a caution. The standard penalty guideline for this offense is a five-place grid drop, but stewards reduced it to **three places**, noting Antonelli did make some reduction in speed and had limited time to react. He'd qualified fourth on raw pace but starts Sunday's race from **P7** as a result. A second, separate investigation was opened over Antonelli allegedly not following race-director instructions to drive at a reasonable pace during qualifying; that one resulted only in a formal warning, not a further grid penalty.
key_points: Stewards hit championship leader **Kimi Antonelli** with **three separate penalties** after Hungarian GP qualifying.
The main charge: failing to slow enough for **yellow flags** thrown when Max Verstappen spun in Q3.
He qualified 4th on raw pace but was dropped **three grid places to P7** for the race.
A second investigation added a **warning** for not following race-director instructions during qualifying.
Stewards said Antonelli did lift off the throttle, just **not enough** — sparing him the harsher 5-place penalty guideline.

depth.background: Yellow flags are shown at a track when there's a hazard ahead (here, Max Verstappen's Red Bull spinning off in Q3, the final and fastest qualifying segment) — drivers are required to slow down meaningfully when they see one, both for safety and to stop anyone gaining an unfair time advantage by racing through a caution zone. Kimi Antonelli has emerged as a genuine title contender this season, part of the storyline the reels covered yesterday about his 'rookie masterclass' during the summer-break report card.

stories.title: India name Sri Lanka Test squad: Jadeja returns, Bumrah in but fitness-watched, Gill captains
stories.what_happened: The BCCI announced India's Test squad for the Sri Lanka tour on Sunday, confirming **Shubman Gill** as captain and **KL Rahul** as his deputy. All-rounder **Ravindra Jadeja** is back in the squad after an extended absence from the format. **Jasprit Bumrah** has also been named, but his participation remains subject to a fitness call closer to the first Test — he's set to report to India's Centre of Excellence after resting his knee until July 30 — with **Mohammed Siraj** and **Prasidh Krishna** rounding out the pace options if Bumrah isn't ready. In the spin department, **Kuldeep Yadav** and uncapped left-armer **Manav Suthar** are the frontline picks. The two-Test series begins **August 15** in Sri Lanka.
key_points: **Shubman Gill** captains the squad with **KL Rahul** as vice-captain for the two-Test tour.
**Ravindra Jadeja** returns to the Test side after last featuring in an ODI back in January.
**Jasprit Bumrah** is included but remains fitness-watched, sharing the pace attack with **Mohammed Siraj** and **Prasidh Krishna**.
**Kuldeep Yadav** and **Manav Suthar** lead the spin options; the series starts **August 15**.

depth.background: India were due to name their Test squad for the upcoming two-match series in Sri Lanka, and the two names everyone was watching were **Ravindra Jadeja**, who hadn't played a Test in months, and **Jasprit Bumrah**, India's premier fast bowler, who picked up a left-knee injury while fielding during an ODI against England in Cardiff on July 17 and had been ruled out of full training until July 30.

thread.previously: As of Sunday, India's Test squad for Sri Lanka was still expected but not yet named, with Jadeja tipped to return and Bumrah's fitness still under review.
thread.changed: The squad has now actually been announced: Gill captains, Rahul is vice-captain, Jadeja is confirmed back in the squad, and Bumrah is named but still fitness-watched ahead of the August 15 series.

stories.title: Cadillac's brake trouble strikes again as both cars retire from the Hungarian Grand Prix
stories.what_happened: Cadillac suffered a double retirement at the Hungarian Grand Prix on Sunday, with both Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez failing to finish. Bottas retired on lap 15 after a fire broke out at his car's left front brake, which he said was caused by overheating that the team's cooling upgrades couldn't fully solve in Hungary's extreme conditions. Perez suffered a separate terminal mechanical issue and also failed to finish. The team had already started the race from the back of the grid — 21st and 22nd — after a difficult qualifying session the day before. This marks the second time this season brake failures have knocked out both Cadillac cars in the same race weekend, after a similar double failure at the Austrian Grand Prix. The team remains without a single championship point through more than half of its debut F1 season.
key_points: Both Cadillac cars — **Valtteri Bottas** and **Sergio Perez** — retired from the Hungarian Grand Prix with mechanical failures, after starting **dead last**.
Bottas retired on **lap 15** after a fire broke out at his car's **left front brake**, caused by overheating.
Bottas said the team's brake-cooling upgrades weren't enough to handle Hungary's extreme conditions.
It's the **second time this season** Cadillac cars have been knocked out by brake failures, after both retired early with the same issue at the **Austrian Grand Prix**.
Cadillac, F1's newest team, remains **without a single championship point** through more than half of its debut season.

depth.background: Cadillac is Formula 1's first new constructor since Haas joined in 2016, entering the 2026 season with backing from General Motors and Ferrari-supplied power units, with long-term plans to build its own engines. New teams typically endure a difficult first season as they learn to build and set up a competitive car from scratch, and Cadillac's rookie year has been rockier than most — reliability, not raw pace, has been the recurring problem, with brake failures already costing the team finishes at multiple races this year.

thread.previously: At Hungarian GP qualifying, Bottas and Perez lined up 21st and 22nd — dead last on the grid — continuing a rough rookie season marked by reliability issues, including brake failures that knocked both cars out early at the Austrian Grand Prix.
thread.changed: The bad qualifying became a bad race too: both cars retired from the Hungarian GP itself, with Bottas's retirement caused by another brake-related failure — a fire at his left-front brake — echoing the exact same problem that hit the team in Austria.

stories.title: Berlin's Pride attack suspect is shot dead by police after a 20-hour manhunt
stories.what_happened: On Saturday evening, a rented van drove into the crowd at Berlin's Christopher Street Day parade near Tiergarten park, killing one person and injuring 29 others. Police identified the driver as Abdul Ballout and launched a manhunt that lasted roughly 20 hours. He was found hiding in a garden in the western district of Spandau on Sunday evening, charged at emergency responders with a knife-like weapon, and was shot dead by police. Prosecutors confirmed his 2025 ISIS-related conviction and his more recent May 2026 arrest for allegedly preparing a violent attack, even though he had remained free. Germany's interior minister and prosecutors say all evidence points to Islamist extremism as the motive.
key_points: A rented van rammed into Berlin's Pride crowd near Tiergarten on **Saturday evening**, killing **one person** and injuring **29 others**.
The suspect, **21-year-old Abdul Ballout**, a German citizen of Lebanese descent, evaded police for **20 hours** before being cornered.
He was shot dead by police in Berlin's **Spandau** district on Sunday after charging at officers with a **bladed weapon**.
Prosecutors say Ballout was convicted in **2025** of trying to join ISIS and was arrested again in **May 2026** over an alleged plot to commit violence.
German officials have labeled it a likely **Islamist terror attack**.

depth.background: Christopher Street Day, Germany's version of a Pride parade, draws large crowds in cities across the country every summer. Prosecutors say Ballout traveled toward Syria in 2025 hoping to join ISIS, was caught and served under two years in prison, then returned to Germany in November 2025. He was arrested again in **May 2026** on suspicion of preparing a serious act of violence, but was not held in custody afterward — a gap that is now central to the fallout from this attack. Berlin has also seen a documented rise in anti-LGBT hate incidents in recent years.

stories.title: Manchester Super Giants thrash Birmingham Phoenix by 87 runs in The Hundred
stories.what_happened: Manchester Super Giants posted 187 for 5 from their 100 balls and then bowled out Birmingham Phoenix for just 100, winning by 87 runs in the competition's 7th match of the men's season.
key_points: Manchester Super Giants posted 187/5 in their 100 balls
Birmingham Phoenix collapsed to just 100 all out in reply
87-run margin is one of the more lopsided results of this year's Hundred
Result strengthens Super Giants' position in the men's competition table

Manchester Super Giants and Birmingham Phoenix are two of the eight men's franchises competing this season.

stories.title: 'How the hell did I end up here?' — Verstappen stunned by his own damaged-car podium as Red Bull says it never gave him a car to attack with
stories.what_happened: After qualifying poorly and picking up car damage during the Hungarian Grand Prix, Max Verstappen finished 2nd — a result he said left him baffled, telling reporters 'I don't understand how we are second' and 'How the hell did I end up here?' Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies backed up Verstappen's surprise, saying the team 'never managed to give Max... a car they could attack with' this weekend and that the car's behaviour was unlike stronger recent races such as Spa or Austria.
key_points: Verstappen said he was 'still shocked' by finishing 2nd after a poor qualifying and race damage
He called it 'a bit of an over-performance compared to what we expected'
Team boss Laurent Mekies said Red Bull 'never managed to give Max... a car he could attack with'
Mekies said this weekend's car behaviour was completely different from stronger races like Spa or Austria

depth.background: Red Bull has struggled with inconsistent car performance across the 2026 season, sometimes competitive and sometimes off the pace from one race to the next, making it hard for the team and Verstappen to predict results race to race. Laurent Mekies, who now leads Red Bull's F1 team, has been managing the team through this stretch of unpredictable form.

stories.title: Toto Wolff launches a 'Teletubbies' rant at rival teams over a blue-flag failure that nearly cost Antonelli the Hungarian GP podium
stories.what_happened: A system fault during the Hungarian Grand Prix meant the automatic blue-flag light panels stopped working, so backmarkers could only be warned manually — and several didn't react in time, holding up Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli as he tried to catch Max Verstappen for 2nd place in the closing laps while defending from Lewis Hamilton behind him. Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff blasted rival teams afterwards, saying it was 'disgraceful' that 'some of the Teletubbies engineers... sitting on the pit walls' failed to tell their drivers what was happening, adding that lapped cars 'defending is just not acceptable.'
key_points: A light-panel system fault meant blue flags could only be shown manually to backmarkers
Antonelli was held up by slow lapped cars while chasing Verstappen for 2nd late in the race
Wolff called rival teams' pit-wall engineers 'Teletubbies' for not warning drivers in time
Antonelli still held on for 3rd, extending his championship lead to 50 points

depth.background: Blue flags are shown to backmarkers (cars a lap or more behind) to tell them to let faster, competing cars past without a fight. Normally this is triggered automatically by trackside light panels, which teams and drivers rely on to know when to yield.

stories.title: West Indies build a commanding 303/7 at lunch on Day 2 of the Pakistan Test
stories.what_happened: Resuming Day 2 from an overnight 194 for 3, West Indies added 109 runs in the first session to reach 303 for 7 by lunch, in 96 overs, despite losing four more wickets along the way. Shai Hope remained unbeaten on 89, anchoring the innings, while lower-order batter Shamar Joseph provided late fireworks with 23 not out off just 12 balls, hitting four boundaries and a six. Pakistan's Aamer Jamal was the most successful bowler in the session, taking a wicket for 81 runs.
key_points: West Indies resumed Day 2 at 194/3 and reached 303/7 by the lunch break
Shai Hope anchored the innings with an unbeaten 89
Shamar Joseph blazed 23 off just 12 balls with four fours and a six
It's a big recovery from a rain-hit 23/1 at the same stage on Day 1

Day 1 was badly disrupted by rain and tight bowling from Pakistan's Mohammad Abbas, which restricted West Indies to just 23 for 1 at the close.

thread.previously: We reported that rain and disciplined bowling from Mohammad Abbas had restricted West Indies to just 23 for 1 at the close of a truncated Day 1.
